job.title: Casual Qualified Matchday Steward
job.html_description:
The Role

We are looking for Casual Qualified Matchday Stewards who hold their level 2 certificate in spectator safety to play a vital role in our matchday operations, fulfilling safety and security duties, providing best-in-class service to stadium attendees and enhancing the supporter and customer experience.

Please note, successful applications will be required to undergo a DBS and Right to Work Check.

Discover why ‘Our Gunners’ are proud to be part of our team - view their stories here.

Who we are

We are one of the most famous clubs in world football, with a rich heritage and history of success – read more about our history, here.

Beyond that, we are passionate about our local community and, behind the scenes, we have a wide variety of opportunities and career paths for all. We have a very defined purpose: to act for a winning team, culture and community. We achieve this by ensuring we are courageous in the pursuit of progress, we champion our community and each other, and that we do the right thing (even when no one is looking).

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed to ensuring that our environments for children, young people and adults at risk remain safe and inclusive. We therefore require successful candidates to complete a DBS check and other essential background checks prior to starting their employment. Depending on the responsibilities of the role, a DBS will be either a basic, standard, or enhanced check.

Your day-to-day

  • Crowd Management: you will deal with all aspects of crowd control and crowd safety from last mile to ingress to circulation through to egress and dispersal, ensuring the safe entry and exit of guests and preventing unauthorised entry into and from the stadium. Reporting any changes in crowd dynamics and being proactive in your approach to handle

  • Safety and Security: you will manage, monitor, and control the safety of all matchday attendees including exit gates, lifts and staircases ensuring clear passage in the event of an emergency.

  • Conflict Management: you'll ensure you are adept at handling conflict and managing queues in a calm and professional manner

  • Customer Service: you will provide an excellent level of customer service for all supporters in matchday attendance, with the ability to communicate effectively, answer queries and accurately provide guidance around the stadium

  • Ticket Checking: you'll actively checking matchday and event tickets to ensure no unauthorised entry into the stadium

What we are looking for

  • Experience: you will have your Level 2 certificate in Spectator Safety

  • Teamwork: you are an effective communicator and team player, more than willing to collaborate and support the members of your team on matchdays to drive success and offer exceptional safety, security, and customer service

  • Proactive: you will have strong attention to detail and ensure all safety and security standards are held throughout

  • Excellent Communication: you will have the ability to clearly communicate with all supporters and guests, providing a positive experience for all attendees in a fast-paced event day environment

  • Committed: you will be prepared to work in all weather conditions

  • Flexibility: you will have availability to work evenings, weekdays, and weekends

Arsenal for Everyone

Arsenal for Everyone is our commitment to promoting and embracing equality, diversity and inclusion, so that everyone connected to the club feels like they belong to the same Arsenal family. We believe that diversity of background, skills and experience drives our success on and off the pitch. 


Disability Confident Leader

We are a Disability Confident Leader. We actively welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a ‘disabled person’ according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment decisions.

Application Closing Date - Tuesday 3rd November 2026

Please note: we reserve the right to close the position early if application volumes are particularly high. We encourage you to get your application in sooner rather than later.

Updates on the status of your application will be sent via email, please routinely check your spam and junk folders, as occasionally emails sent via the Teamtailor platform will find themselves there.

Good luck!

job.title: Community Draw Seller (Casual)
job.html_description:
As a Community Draw ticket seller, you will play a vital role in raising funds for the Cherries Community Fund by selling Community Draw tickets at each home matchday. The Cherries Community Fund is dedicated to providing financial assistance to projects that support young people and vulnerable groups in Bournemouth, Dorset, and Hampshire. 
  • Engage with fans at the stadium prior to kick-off. 
  • Promote awareness of the AFC Bournemouth Community Draw. 
  • Proactively sell Community Draw tickets in designated areas, including outside the stadium and in corporate suites. 
  • Handle payment transactions using card machines. 
  • Collaborate with the Community Matchday Draw Supervisor for any queries or assistance.  
  • As a casual worker you must adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club.  
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures.  
  • Actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 

The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
  • Highly motivated and energetic seller.
  • Ability to positively interact with AFC Bournemouth supporters and fans of the visiting team. 
  • Availability to work weekday evenings, weekends, and Bank Holidays. 
  • Each home matchday 
  • 1.5 hours up to kick-off

job.title: Women's Team Performance Coach
job.location: AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre, Wimborne, Wimborne, Dorset
job.html_description:
To plan, deliver, and monitor physical performance programmes that optimise player readiness, robustness, and availability across the Women’s Football environment (First Team and Development Squad). The role supports long-term athletic development, injury risk reduction, and match performance through evidence-based training aligned with the club’s performance model and relevant league and FA performance support standards.

Women’s Club Values: 
  • Professionalism: Always acting with integrity and respect for the badge in a competent and reliable manner. 
  • Togetherness: Working collaboratively through high levels of communication in a manner that supports an environment where everyone feels included, respected and valued. 
  • Opportunity: Providing fair and equitable chances to all individuals by encouraging a growth mindset through empowering the natural abilities of others in service of the overall mission. 
  • Team First: Prioritising the team beyond personal or individual interests. 
  • Design and deliver gym-based and pitch-based strength, power, speed, and conditioning programmes. 
  • Plan and periodise physical training in alignment with the technical and tactical programme. 
  • Monitor and manage training load, recovery, and physical readiness in collaboration with medical staff. 
  • Support injury prevention strategies and contribute to return-to-play and return-to performance processes.
  • Conduct and analyse physical performance testing and profiling. 
  • Support physical preparation for training and match days. 
  • Contribute to multidisciplinary discussions regarding player availability and performance planning. 
  • Maintain accurate performance data and reporting systems. 
  • Support education of players in training habits, recovery, and physical development. 
  • Support and coordinate the nutritional provision for the women’s team, including supplementation and pre- and post-match / training food, while adhering to anti-doping guidelines and working within the wider multidisciplinary support model. 
  • As a member of staff to ensure in all matters, you follow and actively promote the club’s mental health policies and practices to ensure an open, non-judgmental and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
  • As a member of staff to ensure that you to adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. 
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures.
  • As a member of staff to ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 

The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
Essential
  • Degree in Sport Science, Strength & Conditioning, or a related discipline.
  • Accredited Strength & Conditioning qualification (e.g. NSCA CSCS, UKSCA, ASCA or equivalent).
  • Level 2 Emergency First Aid in Football (EFAIF) or equivalent.
  • Safeguarding and DBS clearance.
  • UK Anti-Doping Introduction to Clean Sport Certificate.
  • Experience delivering strength and conditioning programmes within elite or high-performance sport.
  • Experience working with professional or developing athletes.
  • Experience operating within a multidisciplinary performance team.
Desirable
  • Experience working within professional women's football.
  • Postgraduate qualification in Strength & Conditioning or Sport Science.
  • Experience using GPS and athlete monitoring systems.
  • Knowledge of FA and/or Women's Super League (WSL) performance environments.

Key Attributes 
  • Strong knowledge of strength, power, speed, and conditioning principles.
  • Understanding of football physical demands and match load profiles. 
  • Ability to interpret and apply performance data (e.g. GPS, wellness, testing).
  • Excellent communication and organisational skills.
  • Understanding of female athlete performance considerations.
  • Team-centred and performance-driven approach. 
  • Evidence-informed and detail-oriented practice. 
  • Strong collaborative mindset within an integrated support team. 
  • High professional standards and work ethic.
  • Committed to diversity, inclusion, and the growth of women’s football. 
  • Free onsite parking.
  • Season ticket and allocation of complimentary/purchased tickets (subject to availability).
  • Subsidised lunches and complimentary healthy snacks throughout the day.
  • Discounts at the club Superstore.
  • Access to Health Cash Plan with Simplyhealth.
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Contribution towards eye tests and glasses.
  • Discounts and benefits from partners and local businesses.
  • Club pension & Life Assurance Scheme.
  • Paid parental leave (bank of five days per year).
  • Club events or other social events throughout the year run by our club social team.
  • Paid volunteer opportunities (2 days per year).
  • Paid day’s leave on your birthday.

job.title: Academy Driver (Casual)
job.location: AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre, Wimborne, Wimborne, Dorset
job.html_description:
To transport Academy players to and from all Academy activity, around Bournemouth and nationally.

Academy Values: 
  • Players First: every player valued. Every decision made with care. 
  • Togetherness: working in a prosocial manner as part of a wider team – willing to contribute beyond own interests. 
  • Integrity: carrying out academy and club values in an open and honest manner. 
  • Accountability: willing to take responsibility for actions in a manner which allows learning, growth and reflection. 

  • Transport Academy Players from various pick-up points in the Bournemouth area to and from AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre. Pick up points include but are not limited to: Vitality Stadium, Bournemouth Train Station, Player Accommodation.  
  • Be available to transport Academy players to venues around the country for away fixtures at weekends. 
  • To be available to transport Academy players to other venues as and when needed. 
  • Liaise with the Academy Operations & Player Care teams around weekly schedules and bus registers.  
  • Daily & weekly vehicle checks to be undertaken prior to any journey. Any faults are to be reported in the first instance to the Academy, and maintain the cleanliness of the vehicles. 
  • Provide transport for Academy Players in a safe and lawful manner, fully compliant with the Highway Code and other regulations applying to passenger and minibus transport.  
  • As a casual member of staff to ensure in all matters, you follow and actively promote the club’s mental health policies and practices to ensure an open, non-judgmental and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
  • As a casual member of staff to ensure that you to adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. 
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures.
  • As a casual member of staff to ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
  • Valid UK Driving Licence, including D1 
  • Experience in driving 17-seater minibuses 
  • Experience in driving sports teams or young people (desirable)

job.title: Club Driver
job.location: AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre, Wimborne, Wimborne, Dorset
job.html_description:
To provide a professional, safe and dependable transport service for players, senior management and Club staff, ensuring all journeys are carried out efficiently, discreetly and in line with Club standards. The role is also responsible for maintaining Club vehicles to the highest standards of cleanliness, safety and roadworthiness, supporting the day-to-day operational requirements of the Club.
  • Be available to drive for the Club as required, primarily responsible to football departments and the needs of players and senior management.  
  • Be prepared to work weekends, evenings and other unsociable hours depending on business needs.  
  • At all times, drive safely and follow the highway code, abiding to all speed limits, road signs, etc. 
  • Escorting or aiding players, senior management and other passengers as needed when picking them up or dropping them off at their destination to ensure their safe arrival, comfort and security. 
  • Ensure you arrive punctually for all assigned journeys, planning routes carefully and ensuring enough travel time has been allowed. 
  • Ensure you report any toll charges, congestion charges, drop off charges, etc, to line management punctually so these can be paid on time. 
  • Deliver a consistently comfortable, courteous, and professional driving service, always ensuring discretion and confidentiality. Maintain a high standard of personal presentation, appropriate to the journey you are fulfilling. 
  • Ensure the Club vehicle/s are kept clean, fully valeted, and always presented to a high standard. Keep the vehicle stocked with travel essentials including bottled water, hand sanitiser, first aid kit, etc. 
  • Ensure the Club vehicle/s is kept in a safe and roadworthy condition. This means performing regular vehicle checks and working with the Head of Performance Centre Operations to ensure services, MOTs, vehicle tax, etc, are carried out.  
  • Report any vehicle damage, faults, or maintenance needs promptly to the Head of Performance Centre Operations for action. 
  • In the event you are unable to fulfil an assigned journey, notify the appropriate stakeholder as soon as possible and support with finding an alternative service provider. 
  • Maintain accurate records relating to vehicle usage such as mileage, fuel consumption, service history and other maintenance schedules. 
  • Ensure the vehicle is well always fuelled so at any point; it is available to drive. 
  • Follow all club policies regarding driving company vehicles, insurance and expenses. 
  • As a member of staff to ensure in all matters, you follow and actively promote the club’s mental health policies and practices to ensure an open, non-judgmental and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club.  
  • As a member of staff to ensure that you to adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. 
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures.
  • As a member of staff to ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
Essential 
  • Full clean UK driving license 
  • Experience as a professional chauffeur, taxi driver or other driving career 
  • Good knowledge of Bournemouth/Dorset area 
Desirable 
  • SIA license 
  • Additional driver qualifications / advanced UK driving license 
  • Experience working/interacting with VIPs 


It is anticipated that interviews will be held during the week commencing 9th November 2026.
  • Free onsite parking.
  • Season ticket and allocation of complimentary/purchased tickets (subject to availability).
  • Subsidised lunches and complimentary healthy snacks throughout the day.
  • Discounts at the club Superstore.
  • Access to Health Cash Plan with Simplyhealth.
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Contribution towards eye tests and glasses.
  • Discounts and benefits from partners and local businesses.
  • Club pension & Life Assurance Scheme.
  • Paid parental leave (bank of five days per year).
  • Club events or other social events throughout the year run by our club social team.
  • Paid volunteer opportunities (2 days per year).
  • Paid day’s leave on your birthday.

This means performing regular vehicle checks and working with the Head of Performance Centre Operations to ensure services, MOTs, vehicle tax, etc, are carried out. - Report any vehicle damage, faults, or maintenance needs promptly to the Head of Performance Centre Operations for action. - In the event you are unable to fulfil an assigned journey, notify the appropriate stakeholder as soon as possible and support with finding an alternative service provider. - Maintain accurate records relating to vehicle usage such as mileage, fuel consumption, service history and other maintenance schedules. - Ensure the vehicle is well always fuelled so at any point; it is available to drive. - Follow all club policies regarding driving company vehicles, insurance and expenses. - As a member of staff to ensure in all matters, you follow and actively promote the club’s mental health policies and practices to ensure an open, non-judgmental and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. - As a member of staff to ensure that you to adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. - Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. - Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures. - As a member of staff to ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club.
The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
Essential
- Full clean UK driving license - Experience as a professional chauffeur, taxi driver or other driving career - Good knowledge of Bournemouth/Dorset area
Desirable
- SIA license - Additional driver qualifications / advanced UK driving license - Experience working/interacting with VIPs
It is anticipated that interviews will be held during the week commencing 9th November 2026.
- Free onsite parking. - Season ticket and allocation of complimentary/purchased tickets (subject to availability). - Subsidised lunches and complimentary healthy snacks throughout the day. - Discounts at the club Superstore. - Access to Health Cash Plan with Simplyhealth. - Employee Assistance Programme - Contribution towards eye tests and glasses. - Discounts and benefits from partners and local businesses. - Club pension & Life Assurance Scheme. - Paid parental leave (bank of five days per year). - Club events or other social events throughout the year run by our club social team. - Paid volunteer opportunities (2 days per year). - Paid day’s leave on your birthday.

job.title: Concourse Bar Staff (Casual)
job.html_description:
We are recruiting staff to serve food, confectionery, hot /cold drinks, etc.
 The shifts are approx. 4 - 6 hours home match day only (usually Saturday ko. 3.00pm.).
Staff will be expected to work at a fast pace as we only have a smalltime frame to serve the supporters.

The stadium is very busy on a match day but there is a good atmosphere within the team and you get to know the supporters.

Experience is a bonus, but not essential as full training given onsite.
  • Duties include using tills, recording information, replenishing stock, ensuring your work area is clean and tidy.
  •  You will also be expected to handle food this can include an element of cooking.
  •  You will be expected to work as part of a team as there are 22 concourse bars and kiosk around the stadium.
  • Customer care is very important to us, so you will be expected to be polite and helpful to all individual customers..
  • As a casual worker you must adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. 
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club.

job.title: Chef de Partie (Part Time)
job.html_description:
Join Manchester City Women in a key culinary role supporting elite athletes with high-quality, performance-focused food preparation. Based at the Women’s 1st Team Facility in Manchester, this part-time role offers the opportunity to work in a collaborative environment focused on player wellbeing, recovery and performance.

 

Who We Are

At Manchester City Women, we are proud to be part of City Football Group and one of the leading clubs in women’s football, competing at the highest level in the Women’s Super League, domestic cups, and European competition. Based at the Etihad Campus in Manchester, our team is built on ambition, innovation, and a commitment to excellence both on and off the pitch. We are passionate about developing the women’s game, inspiring the next generation of players and fans, and fostering an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

Our Women’s Team facility team plays an important role in creating a high-performance environment where players and staff can thrive. From daily preparation to match travel support, the team works collaboratively to deliver an exceptional experience that supports health, wellbeing and performance.

The Role

As Chef de Partie, you will support the delivery of nutritious, high-quality meals tailored to the needs of elite athletes and staff. Working closely with the Head Chef, Sous Chef and Nutrition team, you will help ensure food preparation and presentation consistently meets the highest professional standards.

You will contribute to menu development, support smooth day-to-day kitchen operations and help maintain excellent hygiene and food safety practices. The role also includes supporting stock management, reducing waste and maintaining kitchen equipment and service areas.

This is a collaborative role where flexibility and teamwork are essential, including supporting domestic and international travel where required to provide team-standard catering services.

What You’ll Bring

⚽ Experience preparing and presenting food within a professional hospitality or elite sporting environment
⚽ Strong communication and customer service skills with the ability to build positive working relationships
⚽ Knowledge of food safety standards, including HACCP and Food Safety Level 3

⚽ Ability to organise workloads, manage priorities and adapt positively in a fast-paced environment
⚽ Creativity and attention to detail when preparing and presenting food
⚽ Experience supporting stock control, supplier management and minimising food waste

 

Why Choose Us

Working at Manchester City Women means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site, we encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

City Football Group is committed to achieving workforce diversity and we pride ourselves on creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, national origin, race, age, sex, gender identity, disability - physical or hidden, sexual orientation, veteran status, religious belief, or any other characteristics protected by law. We provide a fully inclusive and accessible recruitment process. We encourage all applicants to reach out if they require any support or accommodations to enable them to thrive throughout our recruitment process. Please contact Hiring@cityfootball.com. Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Heating Ventilation Air Conditioning Engineer
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, this permanent role plays an important part in keeping our campus facilities running safely, reliably and to a high standard. You will help maintain and support the mechanical and HVAC systems that underpin day-to-day operations, contributing to a well-managed environment for colleagues and visitors across City Football Group. This role includes occasional weekend and evening work to support football fixtures and events. This role is a static role across campus and does not include transport. 

 

Who We Are

 

Founded in 2013, City Football Group is the world’s leading private owner and operator of football clubs, with teams across the globe connected by a shared belief in doing things differently. Alongside our clubs, we invest in football-related businesses and build partnerships that help the game, and the communities around it, thrive. Everything we do is guided by our purpose: empowering better lives through football. Rooted in more than a century of “City” football, we are proud of the role our clubs play locally and globally, creating positive impact on and off the pitch.

 

Within our maintenance team, we look after the systems and spaces that help the site operate smoothly every day. We work with care, pace and accountability, bringing together practical expertise and collaboration to support a safe, reliable and high-quality environment across the campus.

 

The Role

 

At City Football Group, the maintenance team plays a vital part in keeping our buildings and plant in excellent working order. As Heating Ventilation Air Conditioning Engineer, you will help deliver the maintenance services that support safe, efficient operations across the campus, with a clear focus on standards, safety and reliability.

 

Your work will cover planned preventive maintenance, reactive maintenance and day-to-day inspection of heating, ventilation and air conditioning assets. You will respond promptly to breakdowns, fault-find carefully and support minor installation, upgrade and adaptation works where needed.

 

Working closely with other trades and Maintenance Managers, you will contribute to planned maintenance and life cycle schedules for the buildings on site. This is a hands-on role where good judgement, teamwork and a consistent approach all help keep the campus operating at its best.

 

What You’ll Bring

 NVQ Level 3 in HVAC, Mechanical Engineering or an equivalent qualification

 Valid F-Gas Category 1 certification

 NVQ Level 2 or Level 3 in Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, or an equivalent qualification

 Experience maintaining commercial air conditioning and refrigeration systems

 Experience carrying out planned preventive maintenance and reactive maintenance

 Ability to diagnose faults and respond safely to breakdowns, with a sound understanding of HVAC controls and building services

 

We are also keen to hear from applicants who have the following skills;

  • BMS Knowledge
  • IPAF Licence.
  • PASMA Certification.
  • Experience using CAFM systems.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at City Football Group means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

 

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 20 September 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

We will review applications after the closing date and contact shortlisted candidates about the next stage of the process.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

 

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

 

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

 

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Casual Venue Duty Manager
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, this casual Manchester City role gives you the opportunity to support the delivery of a varied programme of non-matchday events across the Etihad Campus. You will play a key part in making sure each event runs smoothly, feels well organised and reflects the high standards of Manchester City.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

Within our venue operations team, we help bring to life a wide range of events and activations across the Etihad Campus. Our work depends on planning, pace and close collaboration, creating a seamless experience for clients, colleagues and visitors alike.

 

The Role

 

This role sits at the centre of event delivery and gives you the chance to make a visible difference every time the Campus welcomes guests. You will help coordinate the moving parts that keep events running well, acting as a reliable point of contact and making sure each event is set up for success.

Day to day, you will support event set-up and close-down, walk customer journeys, brief teams, and work closely with internal colleagues to make sure requirements are delivered on time. You will also support customer service on event days, handling queries, responding professionally to feedback and helping to maintain a calm, organised and welcoming environment.

You will be trusted to manage event stock control and ordering, including items such as AV equipment, stationery and football equipment, while keeping a close eye on detail and standards. This is a role for someone who enjoys variety, stays composed when priorities change, and takes pride in delivering a smooth experience from start to finish.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽ Experience in events, hospitality or venue operations in a customer-facing role.

⚽ Ability to provide excellent customer service and communicate clearly with clients and colleagues.

⚽ A proactive approach with the ability to work flexibly and adapt to changing priorities.

⚽ Strong organisational skills and close attention to detail.

⚽ Awareness of First Aid and Health and Safety regulations

⚽ Confidence working independently and using your initiative.

⚽ Basic IT literacy, including Microsoft Outlook and Teams.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 25 October 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

We regularly review applications and reserve the right to close the advert early if we identify suitable candidates. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application as soon as possible.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

 

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

 

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

 

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Community Coach - Cross Programme
job.html_description:
Community Coach – Cross Programmes

This Community Coach – Cross Programmes role is an opportunity to make a difference across a wide range of City in the Community programmes. Working with children, young people and communities across Manchester, you will provide flexible, high-quality delivery wherever it is needed most.

 

Who We Are

 

Established in 1986, City in the Community is Manchester City’s official charity. We support people across Manchester by empowering healthier lives through football. Our programmes place physical and mental wellbeing at their core, whilst also creating healthy futures and healthy communities.

 

Across our Education and Community programmes, we use sport, education and positive engagement to support people of different ages, backgrounds and abilities. From schools and education settings to community-based programmes, our teams work across Greater Manchester to create inclusive experiences that help participants develop, achieve and thrive.

 

The Role

 

You will provide flexible delivery support across a range of City in the Community programmes, helping to maintain high-quality provision during periods of staff absence or increased delivery demand.

 

Day to day, you could be delivering across programmes including Early Years, Primary Stars, Inspires, BTEC and Outreach. You will work closely with programme Officers to plan and deliver engaging, inclusive and safe sessions that meet the needs of different participants and programme objectives.

 

Alongside delivery, you will build positive relationships with participants, schools and community partners, support the monitoring of attendance and programme outcomes, and ensure safeguarding and organisational policies are consistently embedded across your work.

 

What You'll Bring

⚽ A minimum NGB Level 2 Coaching qualification in a relevant sport (excluding dodgeball).

⚽ Experience working with children, young people or different groups within the community.

⚽ Experience planning and delivering high-quality, inclusive coaching or education sessions.

⚽ The flexibility and confidence to adapt quickly across different programmes, participants and delivery environments.

⚽ Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to manage delivery and administration across multiple projects.

⚽ A full clean UK driving licence and access to your own vehicle.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Guided by our values of being caring, inclusive, transformative and youth-led, we are committed to creating an environment where our team feel supported, valued and able to make a meaningful difference through the work they do every day.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 23 October 2026.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group is committed to achieving workforce diversity and we pride ourselves on creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, national origin, race, age, sex, gender identity, disability - physical or hidden, sexual orientation, veteran status, religious belief, or any other characteristics protected by law.

 

We strive to provide a fully inclusive and accessible recruitment process. We encourage all applicants to reach out if they require any support or accommodation to enable them to thrive throughout our recruitment process. Please contact citcjobs@cityfootball.com.

 

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Mechanical Workshop Manager
job.html_description:
Based on-site at Manchester CFA, this permanent, full-time role will lead the day-to-day operation of the workshop supporting Manchester City's Grounds and Landscaping team. You will help keep essential machinery safe, reliable and ready to support training, matchday and wider operational requirements. The working pattern is expected to include evening and weekend work.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

Within our Grounds and Landscaping team, we help create and maintain the playing surfaces and landscaped environments that support Manchester City's football operations. Working across Facilities, the team combines practical expertise, careful planning and a shared commitment to keeping our sites safe, well-maintained and ready for the moments that matter.

 

The Role

 

As Mechanical Workshop Manager, you will lead the day-to-day operation of the Grounds workshop, making sure maintenance, servicing and repair work is planned and completed safely, efficiently and to a high standard. Your expertise will help keep the equipment and machinery behind our playing surfaces and landscaped environments available, reliable and fit for purpose.

 

You will plan preventative maintenance, prioritise workshop activity and diagnose mechanical, hydraulic and electrical faults across a varied range of grounds maintenance equipment, machinery and vehicles. You will also coordinate repairs, maintain accurate equipment histories and compliance records, manage stock and spare parts, and raise purchase requests through the agreed procurement processes.

 

Working closely with the Grounds and Landscaping Lead, Grounds colleagues, Facilities teams, suppliers and external service providers, you will provide clear technical advice and updates on equipment availability and repair priorities. You will support equipment replacement planning, identify practical improvements to workshop operations and help maintain a positive culture of safety, good housekeeping and continuous improvement.

 

This is an opportunity to help shape a brand-new mechanical workshop at the City Football Academy. Alongside leading the day-to-day workshop operation, you will support the fit-out and development of a safe, efficient facility equipped for the needs of our Grounds operation. Working closely with the Director of Grounds and other colleagues, you will support the procurement and implementation of equipment including ramps, lifts, grinders, specialist tools and extraction systems, bringing your practical mechanical expertise to the successful delivery of the new workshop.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽ Experience maintaining and repairing grounds maintenance machinery, agricultural equipment or comparable specialist plant.

⚽ Skilled in diagnosing and fault-finding across mechanical, hydraulic and electrical systems.

⚽ Ability to plan and coordinate preventative maintenance activity while prioritising competing operational needs.

⚽ Experience managing workshop stock, spare parts, maintenance records and related documentation.

⚽ Good understanding of health and safety legislation and safe working practices within a workshop environment.

⚽ Relevant mechanical engineering, agricultural engineering or plant maintenance qualification, or equivalent practical experience, with the ability to communicate technical information clearly and use maintenance systems and Microsoft Office applications.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

 

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by Sunday 1 November 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

Our recruitment process will involve standard application screening followed by interview.

Working across Facilities, the team combines practical expertise, careful planning and a shared commitment to keeping our sites safe, well-maintained and ready for the moments that matter.
The Role
As Mechanical Workshop Manager, you will lead the day-to-day operation of the Grounds workshop, making sure maintenance, servicing and repair work is planned and completed safely, efficiently and to a high standard. Your expertise will help keep the equipment and machinery behind our playing surfaces and landscaped environments available, reliable and fit for purpose.
You will plan preventative maintenance, prioritise workshop activity and diagnose mechanical, hydraulic and electrical faults across a varied range of grounds maintenance equipment, machinery and vehicles. You will also coordinate repairs, maintain accurate equipment histories and compliance records, manage stock and spare parts, and raise purchase requests through the agreed procurement processes.
Working closely with the Grounds and Landscaping Lead, Grounds colleagues, Facilities teams, suppliers and external service providers, you will provide clear technical advice and updates on equipment availability and repair priorities. You will support equipment replacement planning, identify practical improvements to workshop operations and help maintain a positive culture of safety, good housekeeping and continuous improvement.
This is an opportunity to help shape a brand-new mechanical workshop at the City Football Academy. Alongside leading the day-to-day workshop operation, you will support the fit-out and development of a safe, efficient facility equipped for the needs of our Grounds operation. Working closely with the Director of Grounds and other colleagues, you will support the procurement and implementation of equipment including ramps, lifts, grinders, specialist tools and extraction systems, bringing your practical mechanical expertise to the successful delivery of the new workshop.
What You’ll Bring
⚽Experience maintaining and repairing grounds maintenance machinery, agricultural equipment or comparable specialist plant.
⚽Skilled in diagnosing and fault-finding across mechanical, hydraulic and electrical systems.
⚽Ability to plan and coordinate preventative maintenance activity while prioritising competing operational needs.
⚽Experience managing workshop stock, spare parts, maintenance records and related documentation.
⚽Good understanding of health and safety legislation and safe working practices within a workshop environment.
⚽Relevant mechanical engineering, agricultural engineering or plant maintenance qualification, or equivalent practical experience, with the ability to communicate technical information clearly and use maintenance systems and Microsoft Office applications.
Why Choose Us
Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.
As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.
Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.
You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.
How to Apply
If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by Sunday 1 November 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.
Our recruitment process will involve standard application screening followed by interview.
We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.
Equal Opportunities
City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.
We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Company Secretary Executive
job.html_description:
Based at the City Football Academy in Manchester, this permanent full-time role supports the delivery of a high-quality company secretarial and governance service across City Football Group's UK and international clubs and companies. Working as part of the Legal team, you will help keep the Group compliant, support effective board and committee operations, and contribute to governance practices that enable the organization to operate with confidence. The role is Manchester-based with flexible hybrid working and regular office attendance.

 

 

Who We Are

 

Founded in 2013, City Football Group is the world's leading private owner and operator of football clubs, with teams across the globe connected by a shared belief in doing things differently. Alongside our clubs, we invest in football-related businesses and build partnerships that help the game, and the communities around it, thrive. Everything we do is guided by our purpose: empowering better lives through football. Rooted in more than a century of "City" football, we are proud of the role our clubs play locally and globally, creating positive impact on and off the pitch.

 

The Company Secretarial function sits within CFG's Legal team and supports the governance of UK and international portfolio clubs and group companies. Working closely with the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary, and the Associate Company Secretary, you will support with board and committee processes, working with colleagues across CFG and helping to deliver company secretarial services in an international football organization.

 

 

The Role

 

As Company Secretary Executive, you will support the Group General Counsel and Company Secretary, and the Associate Company Secretary, with a broad range of day-to-day company secretarial and activities across CFG's portfolio.

 

You will help coordinate board and committee meetings with for example, preparing papers, managing diaries, tracking actions through to completion. You will also maintain statutory registers, company books, share certificates and Companies House filings.

 

The role will involve regular contact with CFG's UK and international corporate services providers, as well as supporting KYC and due diligence requests from banks, regulators and football governing bodies.

 

 

What You’ll Bring

 

A Chartered Governance Institute qualification.

An understanding of UK company law, corporate governance principles and Companies House filing requirements.

Experience supporting boards and/or committees.

 

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at City Football Group means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days' annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 5 November 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

The recruitment process is expected to include an introductory Teams interview of approximately 45 minutes, followed by an in-person interview at the City Football Academy in Manchester with the hiring manager and selected Legal colleagues.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

 

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

 

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

 

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Hospitality Business Development Manager
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, this permanent, full-time role will help grow Manchester City’s matchday hospitality revenue by building relationships with new and existing clients and turning commercial opportunities into high-value sales. You will play a visible part in developing the Hospitality Sales department, creating meaningful client experiences and helping deliver sustainable revenue across each season.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

Within our Hospitality Sales team, we create memorable matchday experiences for clients while supporting Manchester City’s commercial growth. Working across domestic and international markets, the team builds lasting relationships and connects businesses with premium hospitality opportunities at one of the world’s leading football clubs.

 

The Role

 

As Business Development Manager, you will help drive the growth of Manchester City’s Hospitality Sales department by identifying and converting opportunities across our domestic and international client base. Your work will directly contribute to matchday hospitality revenue and to the continued development of relationships with valued clients and prospects.

 

You will build and manage a healthy sales pipeline, maintain accurate reporting and deliver a thoughtful programme of outbound and inbound activity. This will include prospecting, networking, lead generation, referral development, data capture and database management, alongside creating targeted sales strategies and ideas that open up new business opportunities.

 

Success in the role will come from combining commercial focus with a collaborative, service-led approach. You will work closely with colleagues across the department, communicate clearly with stakeholders and represent Manchester City professionally when developing new connections and supporting the client journey.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽ Experience selling high-value products or services to customers or clients.

⚽ Proven ability to build and manage a sales pipeline and work towards commercial targets.

⚽ Practical experience of outbound sales activity, including prospecting, networking, lead generation or referral development.

⚽ Ability to use sales data, reporting and customer information accurately to support decision-making.

⚽ Clear and effective communication and presentation skills, with the confidence to engage a range of stakeholders.

⚽ A proactive, collaborative approach and the ability to contribute positively as part of a team.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

 

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 23 October 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

 

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

 

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Employee Relations Advisor
job.html_description:
Join City Football Group as an Employee Relations Advisor and play a key role in supporting an international workforce. This is an opportunity to work across a broad range of employee relations matters, partnering with managers and colleagues to deliver fair, consistent and people-focused outcomes. 

  

Who We Are 

  

City Football Group is the world’s leading private owner and operator of football clubs, with a mission to empower better lives through football. Built on a vision of sustainability and long-term success, City Football Group brings together clubs, businesses and communities around the world through shared values, innovation and collaboration. 

 
 
You will join our People Team, supporting colleagues across a varied and fast-paced environment. The team works closely with leaders and employees across the organisation to create a positive employee experience and support fair, inclusive and effective people practices. 

  

The Role 

  

As an Employee Relations Advisor, you will provide first-line employee relations support across a wide range of people matters, helping managers and employees navigate processes with confidence and consistency. You will manage a varied caseload including investigations, wellbeing matters, performance discussions and policy-related queries, always balancing a practical and people-focused approach. 

 
 
Working closely with People Business Partners and stakeholders across the organisation, you will contribute to a collaborative and proactive People function. You will also support wider projects and initiatives, helping to strengthen employee relations practices, develop manager capability and provide insights that support continuous improvement. 

  

What You’ll Bring 

  

  • Previous experience in an Employee Relations Advisor, HR Advisor or similar HR advisory role. 

  • Experience managing a busy caseload, across a breadth of HR matters. 

  • Confidence providing advice and guidance to managers.  

  • Experience working within a high-volume HR advisory, or employee relations environment. 

  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise competing demands. 

  • A good understanding of UK employment legislation and HR best practice. 

  • Excellent communication skills with a professional and approachable style. 

  

Why Choose Us 

  

Working at City Football Group means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work. 

 
 
As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance. 

 
 
You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers. 

  

How to Apply 

  

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 1 November 2026. 

  

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

job.title: Attractions Guide
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, these part-time and casual opportunities will see you help deliver engaging Stadium, City Football Academy and Museum experiences for visitors from around the world. You will bring the story of Manchester City to life through confident presentation, warm front-of-house service and memorable storytelling, helping every guest leave with a first-class experience.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

Our Medlock Attractions team welcomes visitors from across the world and creates memorable experiences that bring the Club's history, identity and sense of place to life. Working across tours and the museum, we focus on storytelling, hospitality and creating moments that feel personal, energetic and genuinely memorable.

 

The Role

 

This role is about bringing the Manchester City story to life for visitors from around the world. You will deliver engaging tours across the Stadium, City Football Academy and Museum, using your knowledge, personality and confidence to create an experience that feels welcoming, informative and memorable.

 

Alongside the tours themselves, you will support the wider visitor journey through front-of-house duties, guest meet and greet, museum interactives, visitor flow and the use of tour and museum technology. You will also support other tour products where appropriate and be the kind of guide who notices the small details that turn a good visit into a first-class one.

 

The role calls for someone who can work flexibly, communicate with ease and adapt to a wide range of audiences, from families and children to supporters visiting from across the world. You will be part of a team that represents the Club every day, so consistency, warmth and a genuine sense of pride in the Manchester City experience really matter.

 

Please be aware, we are currently recruiting for part time, and casual, vacancies. Our part time offerings are currently 2 days per week, with at least one of the days worked to include a weekend day.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽ Experience presenting to groups and speaking confidently in front of others.

⚽ Experience working in a customer-facing or visitor-focused environment.

⚽ Experience managing or supporting large groups in a busy public setting.

⚽ Ability to tell stories in an engaging way and adapt your style for varied audiences, including children and family groups.

⚽ A collaborative, flexible approach and the ability to stay calm and positive under pressure.

⚽ Good knowledge of Manchester City, football and Manchester, with confidence using visitor-facing technology.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site before 1st November 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

We will review applications as they are received and contact shortlisted candidates about the next steps.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

job.title: Infrastructure Development Project Manager
job.html_description:
Based at Manchester City's CFA HQ, this full-time fixed-term role will lead the delivery of varied infrastructure projects through to September 2027. You will bring together planning, budgets, contracts and project teams to deliver construction, installation and renovation projects that support internal and external customers, meeting agreed timescales, quality standards and commercial expectations.

 

Who We Are

 

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

Within our Infrastructure Development department, we deliver bespoke infrastructure solutions for internal and external customers. Working across a varied portfolio of projects, the team turns practical requirements into well-planned, well-managed outcomes that support the Club's operations and long-term development.

 

 

The Role

 

 

As Infrastructure Development Project Manager, you will take responsibility for delivering projects across construction, installation and renovation activity. You will shape project plans and requirements briefs, use business and industry intelligence to inform decisions, and lead delivery against agreed budget, programme, specification and quality expectations.

 

You will manage capital budgets and financial modelling, tender projects, and oversee costs, contracts and delivery from inception through to completion. Your work will help ensure that bespoke solutions are commercially sound, practical to deliver and aligned with the needs of the people and teams who will use them.

 

This role involves coordinating project teams and collaborating with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders. You will also look for opportunities to improve commercial and operational outcomes, bringing a thoughtful, organised approach to each project and adapting your delivery as requirements evolve.

 

 

What You’ll Bring

 

 

⚽ Experience delivering projects involving construction, installation or renovation activity.

⚽ Proven ability to plan and control project budgets, including financial modelling and cost reporting.

⚽ Working knowledge of JCT contracts and CDM, including the responsibilities of the Client.

⚽ Ability to develop requirements briefs, manage tenders and coordinate project teams to deliver agreed programme, specification and quality outcomes.

 

 

Why Choose Us

 

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

 

How to Apply

 

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 30 October 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

The recruitment process is expected to include an initial screening interview of approximately 30 minutes, followed by a second-stage interview that includes a presentation. Exact interview dates and format will be confirmed during the process.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

 

Equal Opportunities

 

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

 

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

 

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

 

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.
