job.title: Premier League Primary Stars Coordinator, LFC Foundation
job.location: Anfield Sports & Community Centre, United Kingdom
job.html_description:
We have an exciting opportunity for individuals to join our Liverpool FC Foundation team as a PL Primary Stars Coordinators.

In this role you will support the delivery of the LFC Foundations’ current Premier League Primary Stars Programme and be tasked with delivering classroom lessons for pupils on topics which will include PSHE, English and Maths. You will support the schools by providing extra-curricular clubs, school assemblies, workshops, social action projects, tournaments, competitions and support with transition to secondary schools. You will work with teachers to improve confidence in running PE lessons and work as part of a team across mass participation events.  

The Premier League Primary Stars uses the appeal of the Premier League and Liverpool football club to inspire children to learn, be active and develop important life skills.

What will you be doing?

  • Update LFC Foundation’s reporting database. 
  • Take responsibility for the delivery of the Premier League Primary Stars programme in a designated cohort of schools. 
  • Plan and prepare prior to each session using the PL Primary Stars templates and ensure that careful consideration is given to all abilities, ages, and SEND considerations. 
  • Deliver on the following topics to the highest possible standard across a variety of ages and abilities including: PE, PSHE, English, Maths, Extra-Curricular Clubs, School Assemblies, Workshops, Social Action, Tournament and competitions, Transition to secondary school sessions, Teacher CPD events/sessions and mentoring. 
  • Ensure that all activities are delivered in line with the current primary school curriculum and OFSTED guidelines. 
  • Work closely with primary school teachers to provide support and advice to improve their confidence in delivering PE. 
  • Organise and run teacher training workshops to designated primary schools and staff as part of the PL Primary Stars programme. 
  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with LFC partner schools and their key staff including head teachers, PE coordinators and receptionists 
  • Liaise directly with partner schools to support and promote additional LFC activity 
  • Collect the appropriate monitoring and evaluation documentation for each Premier League primary stars session and assist in the upkeep of VIEWS/Salesforce online monitoring and evaluation. This must be done in a timely and effective manner. 
  • Ensure all activities are correctly monitored with the appropriate risk assessment and health and safety measures. 
  • Willingness to improve through CPD and courses. 
  • The well-being of young people is paramount at the LFC Foundation, you will be expected to understand safeguarding policies and procedures. 
  • Deliver bespoke interventions to individuals or cohorts.     
  • Support holiday camps and half term activation when needed. 

Who are we looking for?

To be successful in this role, you will have a proven track record of delivering sports coaching in schools to young people of all ages and abilities. You will have comprehensive knowledge of the PE national curriculum across KS1 & KS2 and an understanding of different teaching and learning styles. 

You will have excellent communication skills and the ability to build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders. 

Desirable qualifications

  • Hold/Willing to work towards the 1st 4sport level 3 certificate in supporting the delivery of physical education or working towards it.
  • Hold/Willing to work towards 1st 4sport level 2 award in multi-skills development in sport.

Why should you apply?

This role is offering full-time fixed-term contract opportunities for a period of 12 months, working 35 hours per week, on a 5 from 7-day basis including evenings and weekends when required. Your main base will be Anfield Sports & Community Centre, Liverpool however the post holder will also be required to work from other locations across Merseyside from time to time and be willing to travel within England and Wales. 

Please note, this vacancy may close early if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays and the option to purchase up to an additional 5 days) and access to our benefits kit bag which includes but not limited to:

job.title: Development Chef
job.html_description:
We have an exciting opportunity for a talented and creative Development Chef to join our Liverpool FC team.

This is your chance to bring your culinary creativity to life in a fast-paced and innovative environment where great food, fresh thinking and new ideas are at the heart of what we do.

Working from our Central Production Kitchen, you’ll take inspiration from the latest food trends, experiment with new concepts and help develop exciting products from idea through to kitchen. You’ll collaborate with a wide range of stakeholders, sharing your expertise and passion while helping shape our evolving food offering.

You’ll also join a supportive and collaborative team where development is encouraged, with opportunities to learn, upskill and broaden your culinary experience.

What will you be doing?

  • Develop innovative menu ideas, food concepts and product ranges.
  • Research culinary trends and translate insights into new ideas for menus and products.
  • Present findings, run tastings and deliver product showcases for key stakeholders.
  • Create new and exclusive food concepts that support the club’s wider catering offer.
  • Write clear, consistent recipes that can be followed across relevant teams and food categories.
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams, including the Executive Head Chef and Retail Catering team.
  • Ensure that products align with club goals, customer expectations and operational requirements.
  • Support menu development for matchdays, day-to-day catering and retail food products.
  • Comply with all uniform standards as required by legislation and Liverpool FC.
  • Support the recruitment of the kitchen brigade, including full-time and casual colleagues, in line with company and statutory standards.
  • Carry out annual performance reviews with direct reports, ensuring objectives are clear and well defined.
  • Work closely with the hospitality, tourism and events teams to support the delivery of an excellent customer experience.
  • Inspire and motivate the kitchen brigade to deliver high-quality food in line with specifications, while supporting budgeted sales and profit targets.
  • Attend departmental meetings as required and contribute positively as part of the management team.
  • Regularly review the quality and pricing of food suppliers to build strong partnerships and ensure the right products are in place. Suppliers should be audited before appointment and annually thereafter.
  • Meet prospective and existing clients attending events to support the sales process and build effective relationships.

Who are we looking for?

  • Proven current experience as a professional chef, within a busy, multi-site stadium or sports environment.
  • Ability to create and deliver high-quality, innovative recipes across a range of food categories.
  • Strong knowledge of culinary techniques, flavour profiles, ingredients and food trends, with the ability to turn insights into creative food concepts and menus.
  • Confident using Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, to create engaging presentations that inspire stakeholders and communicate new product development ideas.
  • Excellent organisation, communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally and build positive relationships with managers, supervisors, colleagues and customers.
  • Able to work efficiently in a fast-paced kitchen environment, manage time well, work under pressure and use your own initiative when required.
  • High standards of hygiene, presentation and professionalism, with sound recipe-writing practices.
  • Up-to-date knowledge of current food safety legislation, including allergen requirements and Natasha’s Law.
  • Creative approach to problem-solving, with the ability to innovate and stay up to date with changes across the food industry.
  • Ability to plan and lead small events, with flexibility to work occasional evenings when required.

Desirable experience and skills:

  • Experience in a similar role within a football stadium or sports venue.
  • Experience working in a front-of-house environment.
  • Ability to work to strict deadlines in a pressured environment.
  • Budget-writing experience.
  • Ability to speak an additional language.

Why should you apply?

This is a full-time, permanent role working 35 hours per week. Your main base will be our Anfield Stadium. 

Please note, this vacancy may close early if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays and the option to purchase up to an additional 5 days) and access to our benefits kit bag which includes but not limited to:

  • Contributory pension scheme matching up to 5.5%
  • Life Assurance Cover
  • Free financial guidance and mortgage advice
  • Car salary sacrifice scheme for affordable driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme to keep you active
  • Purchase season ticket loans for easier commuting
  • Exclusive shopping discounts & cashback with top retailers
  • Will Writing Service for future planning
  • Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support
  • Medicash Health Cash Plan for everyday healthcare needs
  • Volunteering opportunities to give back to the community
  • Special LFC perks – retail discounts, partner offers, free LFCTV GO access, and priority tickets for matches, events & concerts

…and much more! LFC Benefits.pdf

We take our responsibilities in this area seriously and through the work being done across the club, we are committed to increasing the diversity of our people and becoming an increasingly inclusive workplace for all. We are committed to hiring great people representative of diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills across our entire business. If you share our enthusiasm and passion for inclusivity, then we want to hear from you.

job.title: Events and Fundraising Campaigns Manager (LFC Foundation)
job.html_description:
Events & Fundraising Campaigns Manager (LFC Foundation)

We have an exciting opportunity for an individual to join our LFC Foundation team as a Events & Fundraising Campaigns Manager.

You will lead the planning and delivery of marketing campaigns that promote LFC Foundation’s fundraising events, appeals and engagement activities, driving participation, awareness and income generation. Working closely with the Events & Fundraising team, club departments and external partners, the role will create targeted campaigns that attract new supporters, maximise return on investment and showcase the impact of the Foundation’s work.

What will you be doing? 

Campaign Planning & Delivery

  • Lead and deliver annual marketing campaigns for fundraising events, appeals and engagement initiatives.
  • Develop integrated campaigns that increase registrations, attendance, donations and supporter engagement.
  • Raise awareness of fundraising opportunities and the impact of the LFC Foundation.
  • Grow audiences, attract new supporters and maximise participation and fundraising income.
  • Create targeted campaign plans for events, appeals, corporate fundraising and supporter stewardship.
  • Manage campaign schedules and deliver activity on time.

Revenue & Participation Growth

  • Support fundraising income targets through targeted promotional campaigns.
  • Increase event attendance, participant acquisition and fundraising conversions.
  • Enhance supporter journeys from awareness through to retention.
  • Grow supporter databases and engagement with fundraising products and events.
  • Work with fundraising teams to maximise income-generating opportunities.

Digital Marketing & Audience Development

  • Lead multi-channel campaigns across email, web, social media, paid advertising and partner platforms.
  • Develop campaign messaging, content and creative assets in line with brand guidelines.
  • Create campaign briefs and promotional materials.
  • Use audience segmentation and targeted communications to improve campaign performance.

Stakeholder Management

  • Act as the lead marketer for Events & Fundraising campaigns.
  • Build strong relationships with internal departments and key stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with external agencies, suppliers and media partners to deliver campaigns.

Reporting & Insight

  • Monitor, analyse and optimise campaign performance against KPIs.
  • Produce reports on ROI, participation, awareness and fundraising outcomes.
  • Use supporter insights and campaign data to improve future campaigns.
  • Present campaign results and recommendations to senior stakeholders.

Budget Management

  • Manage campaign budgets effectively and responsibly.
  • Ensure activity delivers measurable ROI and value for money.
  • Monitor and report on campaign spend and performance against budget.

Who are we looking for?

Essential experience, skills and knowledge 

  • Degree or equivalent qualification in marketing and/or relevant course.
  • Significant experience delivering successful integrated marketing campaigns across owned, earned and paid channels including email, web, social media, paid advertising, print marketing and partner channels.
  • Experience driving customer acquisition, engagement or participation through multi-channel campaigns.
  • Experience working with CRM systems, email marketing platforms and digital marketing tools.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple campaigns simultaneously.
  • Experience analysing performance data and using insights to improve campaign effectiveness.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience developing campaign briefs and working with internal creative teams or agencies.
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Experience managing Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) and wider campaign budgets.

Desirable experience, skills and knowledge   

  • Experience within fundraising, events, charity, sports or membership organisations.
  • Experience delivering fundraising or supporter engagement campaigns.
  • Understanding of digital fundraising and supporter journeys.
  • Knowledge of paid social advertising and audience acquisition strategies.
  • Experience working within a football, sport or community organisation.

Why should you apply?

This is a full-time permanent role working 35 hours per week. Your main base will be our Chapel Street, Liverpool city centre office which is close to local bars, shops and restaurants and has great views over the river Mersey.  

Please note, this vacancy may close early if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays and the option to purchase up to an additional 5 days) and access to our benefits kit bag which includes but not limited to:

  • Contributory pension scheme matching up to 5.5%
  • Life Assurance Cover
  • Free financial guidance and mortgage advice
  • Car salary sacrifice scheme for affordable driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme to keep you active
  • Purchase season ticket loans for easier commuting
  • Exclusive shopping discounts & cashback with top retailers
  • Will Writing Service for future planning
  • Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support
  • Medicash Health Cash Plan for everyday healthcare needs
  • Volunteering opportunities to give back to the community
  • Special LFC perks – retail discounts, partner offers, free LFCTV GO access, and priority tickets for matches, events & concerts

…and much more! LFC Benefits.pdf

At Liverpool Football Club, we have an unwavering commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion and are always looking to making a positive difference in the communities that we operate within. We are proud of our achievements in this area; maintaining the Premier League Equality Standard Advanced Level, becoming a founding signatory of the Football Association’s Football Leadership Diversity Code and being recognised as a leader in this important area on and off the pitch. We take our responsibilities in this area seriously and through the work being done across the club, we are committed to increasing the diversity of our people and becoming an increasingly inclusive workplace for all. If you share our enthusiasm and passion for inclusivity, then we want to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Sales Advisor, Chester Store
job.html_description:
We have an exciting opportunity for an individual to join our Liverpool FC team as a Senior Sales advisor. In this role you will work closely with our store management team, in order to drive the store team to ensure excellent customer service and store performance.  

What will you be doing?  

  • Understanding store targets and KPIs to ensure that targets are delivered. 
  • Taking responsibility for running departments within the store and ensuring that all targets are met, and high standards are maintained at all times.
  • Managing the shopfloor, including queues, customer issues, stock availability issues and printing issues, to ensure that high standards are delivered and maintained. 
  • Ensuring all deliveries are received and processed in most efficient manner and the shopfloor is commercially merchandised. 
  • Undertaking keyholder responsibilities, which will include holding the store in the absence of the Store Manager, Assistant Manager & Store Supervisor.  
  • Opening and closing the store, carrying out till counts, investigating, resolving, actioning or escalating any till losses or discrepancies, cashing up, safe counts, banking and managing collections, to complete all of this in accordance with Store standards and compliance checks. 
  • Reviewing the daily handover documents and daily planner to allocate daily activities to the store team, using this detail to talk through the daily brief with the team, providing key targets for the day and allocating sections and/or jobs to the store team. Reviewing that activities are being actioned and follow up as necessary. 
  • Completing customer service observations and floor walks to ensure we maintain high store standards and direct the team to implement any actions. 
  • Supporting with shopfloor moves and any promotional activities and product launches, for example Kit launch and taking responsibility for any key actions in preparation for key launches/events. 
  • Supporting the management team in delivering refresher training to the existing store team, whilst supporting the induction and training of new store team members.

job.title: Senior Specialist, Social Media (Commercial Content)
job.html_description:
We are looking for a Senior Specialist, Social Media to join the team at Liverpool FC. 

This role sits within the Social Media team, part of the wider Creative Content function, and focuses on creating, distributing and optimising commercial content across the Club’s social platforms. Working closely with the Social Media and Commercial Content teams, the role will deliver sponsored and branded content that adds value for club partners while supporting channel growth and engagement.

What will you be doing?

  • Be the social lead for commercial content optimisation and feedback, both internally and externally.
  • Support and optimise partnership ideas/activations and club marketing campaigns to ensure they are suitable for social media in a way that benefits club channels.
  • Shape the club’s global social media presence via commercial content, introducing innovative ideas, formats, and concepts.
  • Partner with internal and external stakeholders, including Content, Graphics, Commercial, and Marketing teams, to develop and deliver branded content and paid social campaigns.
  • Identify social trends, cultural moments, and emerging platform opportunities relevant to our audience.
  • Support the Club’s ambition to remain at the forefront of social media innovation and best practice by monitoring competitor activity and broader industry trends.
  • Utilise research, analytics, and performance measurement tools, working collaboratively with relevant departments to inform and optimise content strategy.
  • Ensure all activity aligns with brand, platform, and partner requirements.

Who are we looking for?

Essential Knowledge

  • Expert knowledge of key social media platforms, including (but not limited to) Facebook, Instagram, X (Twitter), TikTok, Snapchat, YouTube, and WhatsApp.
  • Strong knowledge of LFC’s squads, including players, managers, and coaching staff across men’s, women’s, and youth teams.
  • Proven ability to work within cross-functional media and marketing teams to deliver integrated campaigns.
  • Ability to respond quickly to real-time developments, making confident, informed decisions under pressure.
  • Strong editorial judgement and attention to detail in content creation and publishing.

Essential Functional / Technical Skills

  • Highly collaborative, with experience working effectively across cross-functional teams.
  • Familiarity with social media management platforms for scheduling, approvals, publishing, tagging, and reporting (desirable).
  • Ability to analyse and report on content performance, drawing actionable insights to improve future output.

Why should you apply?

This is a full-time permanent position working 35 hours per week. Your main base will be our city centre office in Liverpool.

Please note, this vacancy may close early if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays and the option to purchase up to an additional 5 days) and access to our benefits kit bag which includes but not limited to:

  • Contributory pension scheme matching up to 5.5%
  • Life Assurance Cover
  • Free financial guidance and mortgage advice
  • Car salary sacrifice scheme for affordable driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme to keep you active
  • Purchase season ticket loans for easier commuting
  • Exclusive shopping discounts & cashback with top retailers
  • Will Writing Service for future planning
  • Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support
  • Medicash Health Cash Plan for everyday healthcare needs
  • Volunteering opportunities to give back to the community
  • Special LFC perks – retail discounts, partner offers, free LFCTV GO access, and priority tickets for matches, events & concerts

…and much more! LFC Benefits.pdf

job.title: Casual Experienced Kitchen Assistants
job.location: Anfield Stadium, Anfield Road Anfield Liverpool, United Kingdom
job.html_description:
Based out of Anfield Stadium, you will be supporting our kitchen operation in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. Play a key role in maintaining high standards of cleanliness, hygiene and food safety, while supporting the wider kitchen team with day-to-day duties. 

This is a casual position offering variable hours on a flexible assignment basis. Due to the nature of the role, shifts may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, and bank holidays, as required.

Who are we looking for?

You will have:

  • Proven experience working as a Kitchen Assistant or in a similar back-of-house role. 
  • Experience working in a fast-paced, high-volume kitchen environment. 
  • Good understanding of kitchen hygiene, food safety and cleaning standards. 
  • Experience operating commercial dishwashers and pot wash equipment. 
  • Ability to safely handle and store cleaning chemicals. 
  • Able to undertake the manual handling requirements of the role, including standing for extended periods and lifting, carrying and moving stock or equipment. 
  • Ability to follow instructions, work effectively with colleagues and work independently when required.

Desirable Skills and Experience

  • Experience working in a stadium, hotel, event venue or similar fast-paced hospitality setting.
  • A Food Safety Level 2 qualification.
  • COSHH awareness or training.
  • Experience with stock deliveries, storage and stock rotation.
  • Experience assisting chefs with basic food preparation tasks.

Due to the nature of this role, applicants must be 18 years of age or over at the time of application. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider applications from anyone under the age of 18 for this role.

Please note: We may close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of suitable applications. We therefore encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Why should you apply?

This is a casual position, offering variable hours including evenings and weekends on a flexible assignment basis.

job.title: ER Advisor
job.html_description:
Working closely with People Partners, line managers and the wider People & Culture function, this role provides practical, hands-on support across employee relations casework and the day-to-day application of People & Culture policies and processes.
 
The role manages a varied caseload, supporting fair, timely and consistent outcomes across disciplinary, grievance, capability, absence and other employee matters. It provides clear advice to managers, maintains accurate case records and works with relevant colleagues to identify and manage employment-related risk. 
 
The role also supports the review and implementation of employment policies and legislative changes, helping translate requirements into clear guidance and workable processes for managers and colleagues. 

What you will be doing: 

Employee Relations

  • Manage a varied Employee Relations caseload, ensuring matters are progressed promptly, fairly and in line with Club policy and employment law. 
  • Provide practical advice and support to managers on disciplinary, grievance, capability, attendance, performance and other employee matters. 
  • Handle complex or sensitive cases, working with People Partners, Legal and other specialists where additional support or escalation is required. 
  • Maintain accurate and complete case records, including correspondence, meeting notes, outcome documentation and case management data. 
  • Monitor case activity and recurring themes, sharing practical observations with the team and People Partners to help improve guidance, processes and manager support. 
  • Apply standard ER processes and controls consistently, supporting fair outcomes and appropriate documentation across all cases. 
  • Keep up to date with employment legislation and case law, working with the in-house Employment Lawyer to reflect relevant changes in advice, guidance and case handling. 
  • Coach and guide managers through individual cases, helping them understand the process, prepare for meetings and make fair, evidence-based decisions. 
  • Support the ER aspects of organisational change, including consultation activity, documentation and individual case support.
  • Support employment status and off-payroll casework, gathering information, coordinating checks and escalating legal, tax or cross-border considerations where required. 
  • Contribute to service improvements by identifying practical ways to simplify case handling, improve templates and strengthen the experience of managers and colleagues. 

Policy and HR Governance  

  • Support the review, drafting and implementation of People & Culture policies and guidance, ensuring they are clear, practical and legally compliant. 
  • Monitor relevant employment law developments and help update policies, processes, templates and manager guidance in response. 
  • Maintain the People & Culture policy library, review schedule and supporting documentation. 
  • Coordinate regular policy reviews and ensure updates are accurately recorded and communicated. 
  • Work with People Partners and subject-matter experts to update policies and guidance in response to case themes, business needs and legislative change. 
  • Provide practical input into policy development, using casework experience to help ensure processes are workable and easy to understand. 
  • Ensure employee-facing policy information and supporting materials are accurate, accessible and current. 
  • Support policy implementation through briefings, guidance and case-based coaching for managers. 
  • Identify policy queries, gaps or inconsistencies arising through casework and raise these with the appropriate policy owner. 
     

Wellbeing and EDI

  • Use Occupational Health referrals and advice to support individual absence, rehabilitation, reasonable adjustment and return-to-work cases. 
  • Coordinate Occupational Health case activity, ensuring referrals are appropriate, reports are followed up and actions are clearly recorded. 
  • Provide practical support to managers handling wellbeing, absence and workplace adjustment matters. 
  • Ensure ER advice and case handling are fair, inclusive and consistent with the Club’s equity, diversity and inclusion commitments. 
  • Work with People Partners, Health & Safety, Impact, Safeguarding and Employee Experience colleagues where individual cases require coordinated support. 
  • Record and share recurring case themes relating to wellbeing, absence and inclusion to support appropriate follow-up activity. 

What we are looking for:

  • ER and Policy management experience with a customer service focus  
  • Proven ability to influence, motivate and support line management  
  • CIPD qualified or equivalent experience 
  • Proven attention to detail, with excellent oral and written communication skills 
  • Excellent communication, influencing and interpersonal skills, with a positive, approachable style and the ability to build strong working relationships. 
  • Commercial acumen with the ability to manage and balance risk 
  • Proven track record of partnering with Senior stakeholders 
  • Comprehensive knowledge of HR policies and practices and employment law 
  • Proven implementer, persuasive and assertive and comfortable with constant change 
  • Resilience and the ability to deal with conflict 
  • Ablity to manage own diary/workload in fast paced environment 
  • Expected to deal with highly sensitive and confidential organisation and employee data 
  • Experience of working in a unionised environment and or/a TU recognition process 
  • Experience of DSAR process  

Please note, this vacancy may close early if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays and the option to purchase up to an additional 5 days) and access to our benefits kit bag which includes but not limited to:

  • Contributory pension scheme matching up to 5.5%
  • Life Assurance Cover
  • Free financial guidance and mortgage advice
  • Car salary sacrifice scheme for affordable driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme to keep you active
  • Purchase season ticket loans for easier commuting
  • Exclusive shopping discounts & cashback with top retailers
  • Will Writing Service for future planning
  • Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support
  • Medicash Health Cash Plan for everyday healthcare needs
  • Volunteering opportunities to give back to the community
  • Special LFC perks – retail discounts, partner offers, free LFCTV GO access, and priority tickets for matches, events & concerts

…and much more! LFC Benefits.pdf

We are proud of our achievements in this area; maintaining the Premier League Equality Standard Advanced Level, becoming a founding signatory of the Football Association’s Football Leadership Diversity Code and being recognised as a leader in this important area on and off the pitch. job.title: Head of Sports Psychology
job.html_description:
This role will lead and deliver an integrated, evidence-informed sport psychology service within Liverpool FC’s football environment. The role will support individual and collective performance, player wellbeing, development and availability by embedding psychological expertise into daily training, competition, rehabilitation and the wider high-performance programme. You will build and lead the wider sports psychology methodology and provision at the club.

What you will be doing:
INDIVIDUAL PLAYER PERFORMANCE AND SUPPORT 

  • Provide confidential one-to-one sport and performance psychology support to Men’s First Team players, tailored to individual performance and development needs. 
  • Develop and review individual psychological performance plans aligned with player objectives, coaching priorities and the wider interdisciplinary performance plan. 
  • Build players’ psychological skills in areas including confidence, focus, emotional regulation, decision-making, coping with pressure, preparation and performance routines. 
  • Support players through selection and non-selection, injury, rehabilitation, return to performance, loss of form, major fixtures, career transitions and other high-demand periods.
  • Maintain clear professional boundaries and facilitate timely referral where specialist clinical mental-health or other support is required. 

TEAM, TRAINING AND MATCH PERFORMANCE 

  • Design and deliver squad interventions across the season in response to identified team, performance and competition needs. 
  • Embed practical psychological principles within training design, competition preparation, matchday processes, recovery and post-match learning. 
  • Support leadership, communication, cohesion, collective resilience, role clarity and the behaviours required within an elite First Team environment. 
  • Work closely with the Head Coach and coaching staff to translate psychological concepts into relevant, practical and football-specific approaches. 
  • Provide psychologically informed support during periods of intense fixture congestion, decisive competition phases, change and heightened external scrutiny. 

COACH, STAFF AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY SUPPORT 

  • Provide trusted sport psychology consultation to the Head Coach, coaching staff and members of the Men’s First Team leadership group. 
  • Operate as an integrated member of the Medical and Performance multidisciplinary team, contributing to appropriate player, availability, rehabilitation and performance meetings. 
  • Collaborate with Medical, Physical Performance, Nutrition, Performance Analysis, Coaching and Player Care colleagues to deliver coordinated player support. 
  • Provide education, guidance and practical resources that increase the capability of coaches and staff to create psychologically informed learning and performance environments. 
  • Contribute psychological expertise to player development, readiness and return-to-performance discussions while protecting consent, confidentiality and professional boundaries. 
     

HIGH-PERFORMANCE ENVIRONMENT AND CULTURE 

  • Support the Director of Medical and Performance and wider First Team leadership in developing a psychologically informed, player-centred high-performance environment. 
  • Promote effective communication, accountability, learning, psychological safety and appropriate professional behaviours across the daily performance environment. 
  • Contribute to the development of player leadership, ownership and self-regulation while respecting the standards and demands of Men’s First Team football. 
  • Build credible, trusted relationships across a diverse, international playing and staff group, adapting communication to different cultures, experiences and needs. 
  • To build and lead the wider Sports Psychology methodology and provision at the Club.

PROFESSIONAL GOVERNANCE, MONITORING AND DEVELOPMENT 

  • Practise in accordance with HCPC standards and all relevant professional, legal, safeguarding and Club requirements. 
  • Maintain appropriate confidential records, informed-consent processes, information sharing and referral pathways, ensuring practice remains within professional competence and scope.
  • Maintain HCPC registration, appropriate professional supervision, reflective practice and continuing professional development throughout employment. 
  • Develop an annual psychology delivery plan aligned to Men’s First Team and Medical and Performance priorities, with proportionate evaluation of reach, quality and impact. 
  • Provide the Director of Medical and Performance with appropriate service-level updates, emerging themes and priorities without compromising individual confidentiality. 
  • Contribute to innovation, applied research and evidence-informed practice that strengthens the Club’s performance support provision.

What we are looking for:

  • Postgraduate qualification in Sport and Exercise Psychology, or an equivalent relevant discipline. 
  • Current HCPC registration as a Practitioner Psychologist, with appropriate competence to practise in sport and exercise psychology, and relevant professional accreditation or chartered status where applicable.
  • Substantial applied experience delivering sport psychology within elite or high-performance sport, ideally in a senior or lead practitioner capacity. 
  • Demonstrable experience supporting elite athletes individually and delivering team-level interventions in high-pressure performance environments. 
  • Experience working effectively with senior coaches and within multidisciplinary medical and performance teams. 
  • Strong working knowledge of professional ethics, confidentiality, informed consent, safeguarding, record keeping, clinical referral pathways and information governance. 
  • Evidence of ongoing professional supervision, reflective practice and continuing professional development.
  • Ability and willingness to work flexibly around the demands of elite football, including training, matchdays, travel, evenings and weekends as required. 

DESIRABLE EXPERIENCE 

  • Applied experience within men’s professional football, preferably in a First Team environment. 
  • Experience supporting players through injury rehabilitation and return to performance in collaboration with medical and physical performance practitioners.
  • Additional training or demonstrated competence in evidence-based psychological approaches relevant to elite sport.
  • Experience designing, monitoring and evaluating an integrated psychology service across a full competition season. 
  • Research experience or established links with higher education and applied sport psychology networks. 

Please note, this vacancy may close early if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To reward your hard work and commitment we offer a competitive salary, 25 days holiday (plus 8 bank holidays and the option to purchase up to an additional 5 days) and access to our benefits kit bag which includes but not limited to:

  • Contributory pension scheme matching up to 5.5%
  • Life Assurance Cover
  • Free financial guidance and mortgage advice
  • Car salary sacrifice scheme for affordable driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme to keep you active
  • Purchase season ticket loans for easier commuting
  • Exclusive shopping discounts & cashback with top retailers
  • Will Writing Service for future planning
  • Employee Assistance Programme for confidential support
  • Medicash Health Cash Plan for everyday healthcare needs
  • Volunteering opportunities to give back to the community
  • Special LFC perks – retail discounts, partner offers, free LFCTV GO access, and priority tickets for matches, events & concerts

…and much more! LFC Benefits.pdf

At Liverpool Football Club, we have an unwavering commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion and are always looking to making a positive difference in the communities that we operate within. We are proud of our achievements in this area; maintaining the Premier League Equality Standard Advanced Level, becoming a founding signatory of the Football Association’s Football Leadership Diversity Code and being recognised as a leader in this important area on and off the pitch. We take our responsibilities in this area seriously and through the work being done across the club, we are committed to increasing the diversity of our people and becoming an increasingly inclusive workplace for all. We are committed to hiring great people representative of diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and skills across our entire business. If you share our enthusiasm and passion for inclusivity, then we want to hear from you.

Liverpool FC is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and vulnerable adults and expects all Colleagues and Volunteers to share this commitment. This role is subject to a satisfactory enhanced DBS check.

job.title: Academy- Lead Athletic Development Coach
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
NO PHONE CALLS OR EMAILS, PLEASE.  Thanks for your interest! Due to the volume of applications, we’re unable to respond to individual status inquiries. If selected to move forward, you’ll hear from our HR team at Nashville Soccer Club.

POSITION OVERVIEW
The Athletic Development Coach will lead the Long-Term Athletic Development (LTAD) program for the Nashville SC Academy in alignment with the High Performance philosophy. This role works closely with High Performance staff across NSC and HCFC to design and implement team and individual programs, both in the gym and on the field, to optimize youth athlete development.
The ideal candidate has coaching or strength & conditioning experience, formal education in exercise physiology or a related field, and expertise in load management for youth soccer.
This position reports to the Director of High Performance and the Head of Athletic Development for the First Team, and collaborates with the Academy Director, Athletic Trainers, and performance staff to support a collaborative, high-performance environment.
This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the development of elite youth soccer players!
 
RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead and oversee on-field warm-ups, cool-downs, strength training, and prehabilitation sessions, as well as individualized training for targeted or rehabilitating players in collaboration with medical staff.
  • Design and implement individual and team off-season training programs.
  • Foster strong relationships with players and staff to effectively deliver performance programs.
  • Develop educational materials to promote best practices in athletic development and sport performance, aligning with the High Performance department’s initiatives.
  • Organize and maintain field and gym equipment.
  • Travel with the team to games and events as needed.
  • Stay current with the latest research and best practices for future program implementation.
  • Contribute to and enhance LTAD programming, including data collection, testing, analytics, and reporting to optimize youth player performance.
  • Manage player performance data, including distributing devices, processing and inputting data, wellness monitoring, testing administration, RPE collection, analysis, and reporting.
  • Utilize performance monitoring tools and technologies to track player performance and support injury prevention strategies.
MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
  • Undergraduate (Bachelor’s) Degree from a 4-year accredited University in related field of study such as Kinesiology, Exercise Science, Sport Science, Biomechanics, Strength & Conditioning, and/or similar
  • NSCA-CSCS (Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist)
  • CPR Certification

PREFERRED

  • Graduate (Master’s) Degree from an accredited University in related field of study
  • 2-3 years experience working with youth soccer within the United States
  • NSCA-CPSS (Certified Performance and Sport Scientist)
  • Functional Movement Screening (FMS) and Selective Functional Movement Assessment (SFMA) Level 1
  • Bilingual in English and Spanish
 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

job.title: Team Operations - Performance Scientist
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
NO PHONE CALLS OR EMAILS, PLEASE.  Thanks for your interest! Due to the volume of applications, we’re unable to respond to individual status inquiries. If selected to move forward, you’ll hear from our HR team at Nashville Soccer Club.

Position Title: Performance Scientist

Department: Team Operations- High Performance

Reports to: Director of High Performance

 

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Performance Scientist supports player availability and performance by leading sport science data operations, monitoring, reporting, and applied insights that inform training, recovery, and return-to-performance decisions. This role reports directly to the Director of High Performance and works in close collaboration to define the path forward for key initiatives. The Performance Scientist will be provided autonomy to determine the best execution plan, while ensuring alignment with coaching, performance, and medical priorities.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own end-to-end sports science data operations (collection, QA/QC, documentation, and governance) across performance data streams.
  • Lead training and match monitoring systems (e.g., STS) and related technologies (GPS, heart rate, VALD, 1080 and others), ensuring reliable workflows and clean outputs.
  • Build and maintain dashboards, models, metrics, and reports that track workload, readiness, and physical performance across the season.
  • Deliver clear, actionable insights to coaches, performance/medical staff, and players (including real-time training feedback when needed).
  • Plan and execute performance testing and assessment protocols (field and gym-based); maintain benchmarks and individualized targets.
  • Collaborate with Athletic Development and Medical on activation, strength/regeneration, and end-stage return-to-performance support as needed.
  • Partner with analytics and scouting on performance questions tied to player evaluation, transactions, and projections.
  • Lead integration of second team and academy performance data into centralized systems, standards, and reporting.
  • Ensure compliance with all MLS medical manual requirements and club policies and procedures.

KEY DELIVERABLES

  • Readiness/availability updates aligned with training plans and performance/medical direction.
  • Stakeholder dashboards and reports with clear KPI definitions and refresh cadence.
  • Testing battery execution and reporting with benchmarks, targets, and action steps.
  • Multi-squad integration outputs (first team/second team/academy) using shared standards and longitudinal tracking.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree in Exercise Science or related field.
  • Certified Performance and Sport Scientist (CPSS).
  • Certified Strength and Conditioning Specialist (CSCS).
  • Minimum 2 years experience in an elite sport environment.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with GPS systems, heart rate, force plates, and current performance technologies.
  • Experience in a coach-facing role explaining monitoring outputs and real-time GPS results.
  • Proficiency in R, Python, and Power BI for data analysis and reporting.
  • Current CPR/AED certification (or ability to obtain promptly).

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience querying cloud databases and supporting automated/real-time reporting (e.g., SQL, ETL, APIs).
  • Comfortable conversing in Spanish.
  • Experience scaling sport science systems across multiple squads (first team + second team + academy).
  • Strong data QA habits and reproducible workflows (e.g., documentation, version control).

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

job.title: Ticketing - Box Office Representative PT
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
POSITION OVERVIEW
The Ticket Office Representative is a part-time, event-day position responsible for providing exceptional customer service and assisting fans with ticket purchases and inquiries at GEODIS Park. This role plays an important part in delivering a seamless matchday experience by supporting ticket sales, processing transactions, and resolving ticket-related questions. Applicants must reside in the Nashville area.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Process ticket sales through Ticketmaster and assist guests with ticket purchases and ticketing issues.
  • Provide clear, friendly, and professional customer service throughout all interactions.
  • Address general inquiries related to seating options, pricing, stadium policies, and event information.
  • Accurately complete credit card and cash transactions in accordance with Club procedures.
  • Reconcile and balance cash drawers at the end of each shift.
  • Support Box Office leadership with additional duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS
  • Prior customer service or ticketing experience preferred, but not required.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to remain professional in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to learn and navigate ticketing software quickly (experience with Ticketmaster is a plus).
  • Reliable, punctual, and able to work Nashville SC home matches, special events, nights, weekends, and holidays as needed.
  • Must be detail-oriented and comfortable handling cash and sensitive customer information.
  • Candidates without a degree are encouraged to apply.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

job.title: Backup Mascot
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
Nashville SC is looking for highly motivated individuals interested in being a part of the Major League Soccer team in Nashville. The ideal candidates will demonstrate initiative, the ability to multi-task, a willingness to learn and a positive attitude. Please note: This is a part-time, as needed Backup position.

Employment Type: Part-Time

 

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

· Study and learn Tempo the Coyote's mannerisms and characteristics

· Assist Tempo the Coyote at home matches

· Provide support at select appearances, including birthday parties, parades, school visits, hospital visits, charitable events, and other events coordinated by Tempo the Coyote

· Assist in maintaining the condition of costumes and props

· Other duties as assigned by Tempo the Coyote

· Please note this is a part-time, as needed Backup position.

 

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

· Knowledge and interest in sports.

· Knowledge and interest in mascots.

· Computer proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

· Proficient in social media.

· Strong communication skills and telephone etiquette.

· Mascot Experience (College or Professional)

 

REQUIREMENTS:

· Available as needed for Tempo the Coyote appearances.

· Available to assist with home matches.

· The understanding that working in sports is different than being a fan. This position does not guarantee candidates will be able to watch games. Many valuable positions within the organization are behind the scenes, and they provide little ability to watch the games.

· Tempo the Coyote Height Range: 5'7 - 5'10.

 

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

· Other duties as assigned by Tempo the Coyote
· Please note this is a part-time, as needed Backup position.
DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:
· Knowledge and interest in sports.
· Knowledge and interest in mascots.
· Computer proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
· Proficient in social media.
· Strong communication skills and telephone etiquette.
· Mascot Experience (College or Professional)
REQUIREMENTS:
· Available as needed for Tempo the Coyote appearances.
· Available to assist with home matches.
· The understanding that working in sports is different than being a fan. This position does not guarantee candidates will be able to watch games. Many valuable positions within the organization are behind the scenes, and they provide little ability to watch the games.
· Tempo the Coyote Height Range: 5'7 - 5'10.
We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

job.title: Youth Soccer Coach - Part Time
job.html_description:
Position Summary
Nashville Soccer Club is seeking energetic, reliable, and knowledgeable coaches to support the delivery of its Youth Soccer Programs. This role focuses on camps, clinics, grassroots programming, Academy pathway programs and coach education initiatives across the Nashville community. The role is centered on player development programming within the Youth Soccer Department. Coaches will represent Nashville SC while delivering high-quality soccer experiences that are fun, inclusive, and developmentally appropriate. This position is part-time, with flexible scheduling based on program needs, including evenings, weekends, and seasonal peak periods. Strong performers may be considered for expanded responsibilities or future full-time opportunities within the club. This is not an academy coaching position.

Duties & Responsibilities
  • Deliver engaging and age-appropriate coaching sessions at camps, clinics, and grassroots programs.
  • Implement Nashville SC Youth Soccer curriculum and session plans across all youth programming.
  • Create a positive, safe, and inclusive environment for all participants.
  • Support event operations including setup, check-in, and breakdown of sessions.
  • Serve as a club ambassador, maintaining professionalism with players, parents, and partners.
  • Assist with coaching education sessions and mentorship initiatives when required.
  • Provide feedback on player development and program delivery when requested.
  • Ensure all safety, risk management, and safeguarding standards are followed.
Qualifications
  • Previous coaching experience in youth soccer (recreational, grassroots, or club level required).
  • Passion for working with children and developing players of all ability levels.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work flexible hours including evenings and weekends.
  • Reliable transportation to program locations across the Greater Nashville area.
  • US Soccer Grassroots (or equivalent) License or higher (or willingness to obtain).
  • Experience working in a youth development environment (Rec, Club, Academy or camps).
  • Background in player development models.
  • Ability to be active for extended periods (standing, running, demonstrating drills)
  • Ability to lift and carry equipment up to 30 lbs

job.title: Soccer Squad (Part-Time)
job.html_description:
Position Summary:
Nashville SC Soccer Squad will serve as community ambassadors for the Club at key community-based events and programs throughout Nashville. This group will be integral to executing community outreach through soccer programming. The Soccer Squad will also serve as an extension of the Community Engagement department by assisting with our core youth soccer programs including Grassroots Soccer, IMPACT Soccer, MNPS P.L.A.Y.S., and more.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities:
  • Facilitate soccer-specific activations at community engagement events while providing superb customer service and displaying excitement about the organization.
  • Act as an extension of the club’s community engagement department by providing information on various soccer programs.
  • Assist with program set-up and breakdown. 
  • Collect and report valuable feedback and insights after each event to provide back to the team supervisors.
Shift Information:
  • Must be able to work flexible hours including evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Some shifts will require picking up materials to transport to the event site, plus setting up and taking down materials.
Qualifications:
  • A general interest and working knowledge of the sport of soccer. 
  • Should be able to answer basic questions about the game, NSC’s schedule and roster, etc.
  • Experience playing the game and coaching youth is preferred but not required.
  • Strong people and communication skills. 
  • Comfortable promoting and interacting with new people at NSC events with a fun and positive attitude.
  • Collaborative personality who works well with others on their team. 
  • Enjoys engaging with team members and is responsive to messages.
  • Must have transportation, a good driving record, and valid driver’s license.
  • Reliable and punctual, being on-time is important to you.
  • Bilingual (English & Spanish) is helpful but not required.
  • Must be able to move and lift a minimum of 50 pounds.
  • Background check is required.

job.title: Academy- Goalkeeper Coach PT
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
NO PHONE CALLS OR EMAILS, PLEASE.  Thanks for your interest! Due to the volume of applications, we’re unable to respond to individual status inquiries. If selected to move forward, you’ll hear from our HR team at Nashville Soccer Club.

POSITION OVERVIEW:
The Academy Part-Time Goalkeeper Coach will be responsible for the U14 and U15 academy goalkeepers. The goalkeeper coach will be tasked with constructing and executing individualized goalkeeper sessions as well as assisting head coaches on the field where necessary. This person will work closely with the Academy Goalkeeper coach, as well as academy staff and must adhere to all club and league requirements. The ideal candidate must have previous experience in the role of goalkeeper both as a player and coach.

RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Be able to work roughly 20 hours per week, mainly afternoon sessions with our younger age groups- U14 and U15 boys.
• Construct and execute individualized goalkeeper sessions geared towards our style of play and model
• Assist with Head coach needs during a training session
• Actively participate in player individualized meetings and communicate with academy goalkeepers
• Availability to attend home matches on the weekend on a need basis
• Complete Club and League registration requirements including background checks, SafeSport, Heads up.
QUALIFICATIONS:
• Playing and coaching experience in the Goalkeeper position
• Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
• Strong ability to communicate and work under pressure.
• Passion for youth soccer and knowledge of MLS
• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience preferred.
• Ability to speak Spanish is a plus.

job.title: Academy- Assistant Performance Coach PT
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
NO PHONE CALLS OR EMAILS, PLEASE.  Thanks for your interest! Due to the volume of applications, we’re unable to respond to individual status inquiries. If selected to move forward, you’ll hear from our HR team at Nashville Soccer Club.

POSITION OVERVIEW
The part-time Assistant Performance Coach for the Nashville SC Academy will be responsible for supporting and assisting the club by providing an integrated High-Performance LTAD program for it’s Academy players, in line with the Club and Performance department philosophy. This position will work closely with the Academy Director, Academy Performance Coach, and Academy Medical Department to create team and player-specific programs and administer those programs on the field and in the gym for developing youth athletes within the Academy. The person in this role should have prior playing and/or coaching experience and be expected to comfortably facilitate soccer-centric programs.  In addition, they should also have a formal educational background in exercise physiology (or similar degree) and load management across a variety of metrics as it relates to the development of youth soccer athletes.  This role will report directly to the Head of Performance for the First Team and will work closely with the Academy Director, Academy Performance Coach and Academy Athletic Trainer, as well as various other key coaches/staff.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • This position will direct and/or assist in the following areas:
  • Assisting, managing and directing on-field warm up and cool down sessions, strength training, prehabilitation, as well as individual sessions for targeted or rehabilitating players in conjunction with medical staff
  • Distribution of player devices and processing data into club systems on a daily basis, along with wellness monitoring, testing administration, RPE collection, compiling, analysis, and reporting
  • Utilizing various monitoring software, tools and technologies to report on player performance and injury prevention
  • Direct and/or assist with the delivery of scientifically based optimal recovery strategies post trining and post-match
  • Help develop and implement individual and/or team off-season programs
  • Help develop strong interpersonal relationships with players and staff to effectively administer programs
  • Help producing educational materials for players to guide towards best practices in the development and optimization of sport performance
  • Organizing and maintaining field and gym equipment
  • Surveying literature and best practices for future implementation
  • Contribute to and advance LTAD programming and curriculum, data collection, testing, analytics, and reporting to develop high-performance in youth players
  • Occasional travel with team to games/events

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
  • Undergraduate (Bachelor’s) Degree from a 4-year accredited University in related field of study such as Kinesiology, Exercise Science, Sport Science, Biomechanics, Strength & Conditioning, and/or similar
  • NSCA-CSCS (Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist)
  • CPR Certification
PREFERRED
  • Graduate (Master’s) Degree from an accredited University in related field of study
  • 2-3 years experience working with youth soccer within the United States
  • XPS-EXOS Performance Specialist
  • Functional Movement Screening (FMS) – Certified Level 1/2
  • Bilingual in Spanish and English
HOURS
  • 15-20 hours per week
  • Nights and weekend availability
 

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

job.title: Marketing - Street Team PT
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
Position Summary
Nashville SC Street Team members serve as key community ambassadors for the Club throughout the 2025 season. This role supports fan engagement at public appearances, home matches, away watch parties, and community events across the Nashville area. Street Team members play a vital role in strengthening fan loyalty by enhancing the matchday and event experience, while also serving as an extension of the Club’s Marketing and Entertainment teams.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities
  • Facilitate on-site activations and promotional events while delivering exceptional customer service and representing the Club with energy and professionalism.
  • Serve as an extension of the Marketing Department by promoting club initiatives, ticket programs, and brand messaging.
  • Assist guests as part of the GEODIS Park guest experience team when needed.
  • Actively engage with fans to encourage participation in activations, distribute giveaways, and provide event-specific information.
  • Assist with the setup, operation, and breakdown of interactive displays, promotional booths, and event materials.
  • Distribute marketing collateral in an organized and professional manner.
  • Collect and report feedback, observations, and insights following events to supervisors.
  • Support pre-match activities, including Opening Act activations (e.g., Kick Wall, premium tailgate).
  • Serve as a matchday runner for the Nashville SC Entertainment team as needed.
  • Assist with matchday entertainment management, hospitality, and game presentation needs.
  • Support production logistics, including entertainment personnel arrival, load-in, and load-out.

Shift Information
  • Shifts include all home matches, the majority of away matches, and additional off-site community events throughout the season.
  • Hours vary by event schedule, with an expected commitment of approximately 5–15 hours per week during the season.
  • Some shifts require transporting materials to and from event locations and assisting with setup and teardown.

Qualifications
  • Ability to commit to all Nashville SC matchdays (home and away) with minimal scheduling conflicts.
  • General interest in and working knowledge of soccer, including basic understanding of Nashville SC’s schedule and roster.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills with a positive, outgoing attitude.
  • Comfortable engaging with fans and promoting club initiatives in public settings.
  • Team-oriented, collaborative mindset.
  • Willingness to learn club promotions, ticket programs, and soccer-related information (training provided).
  • Reliable transportation, valid driver’s license, and a good driving record.
  • Availability to work evenings, weekends, and select holidays.
  • Dependable, punctual, and professional.
  • Ability to lift and move materials exceeding 50 lbs.
  • Ability to maintain professionalism when interacting with VIP-level personnel.
  • Bilingual (English/Spanish) preferred but not required.
  • Prior experience in promotions, events, or brand ambassador roles preferred.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

job.title: Housekeeping - Housekeeping PT
job.location: GEODIS Park, 2226 Bransford Ave, Nashville, Tennessee, United States of America
job.html_description:
About Nashville SC & GEODIS Park:
 Nashville is America’s “It City” and one of the fastest-growing soccer hubs in the country. From hosting the CONCACAF Gold Cup to FIFA World Cup Qualifiers and the FIFA Club World Cup, Music City has quickly become a destination for some of the sport’s most prominent events. Locally, Nashville SC is in its sixth season and continues to thrive both on and off the field, highlighted by the opening of GEODIS Park in May 2022—the largest soccer-specific stadium in Major League Soccer. 
 
What we are looking for:
  • Individuals available for 6-8 hours, 15-20 times per year, and available to attend all necessary in-person and virtual training as a prerequisite for employment
  • Someone who enjoys speaking and interacting with others in a warm, and respectful manner
  • Must enjoy helping others and working within a team environment
  • Ability to lift, pull, push and/or carry 25-60 lbs. as necessary
  • Must be able to stand for long periods of time and be exposed to different types of weather 

Primary roles & responsibilities:
  • Maintain stadium cleanliness, emptying trash cans, replacing trash cans with a new liner, wiping down countertop areas, tops of trash cans; sweeping/mopping the concourse as necessary; squeegeeing standing water to provide a safe environment for our guests; picking up and throwing away trash left in the stadium and outside perimeter that cannot be swept.
  • Responsible for providing a clean and safe facility before, during, and after all events
  • Responsible for picking up trash and emptying trash and recycle receptacles
  • Maintain all aspects of restroom cleanliness and preparedness by stocking and wiping down dispensers; cleaning and disinfecting all fixtures (toilets, urinals, sinks, baby changing tables); keeping the floor clean, dry and free of debris; and emptying trash cans
  • Respond to and resolve guests’ questions, concerns, complaints or suggestions in a professional and polite manner. Recognize and respond effectively in emergency situations
  • Supervisory positions available
