job.html_description: U.S. Soccer OverviewThe U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.Position Description As the first Legal Operations Specialist at U.S. Soccer, you will help our Legal department run core functions like document management, contract lifecycle management, legal billing and budgeting, technology and vendor management, and routing incoming correspondence. Just as important, you will partner with Legal leadership to improve operational efficiency, enable data-driven decision-making, and get more out of our technology, including AI-enabled tools.  This is a great opportunity to build the legal infrastructure of a rapidly growing department and make an impact across the organization. You won’t find a typical legal operations job here! You will join a collaborative team that values mentorship and high standards, supporting a national governing body during a period of tremendous growth and ambition. Expect a fast pace, a casual work environment, and a front-row seat to the work of growing soccer in America. The ideal candidate has legal operations experience, a passion for organization and efficiency, and excitement for building processes and systems. You stay calm in the face of chaos and aren’t afraid to challenge the status quo.  This full-time, non-exempt position is based at our national training center in Fayetteville, GA. We currently operate on a hybrid schedule, with in-office days every Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.Primary ResponsibilitiesDocument Management  Own our document management system and ensure that files are properly stored, named, and organized. Develop and maintain a cross-functional contract database. Receive and route physical legal mail. Process Management & Improvement Improve and streamline legal department processes by identifying, assessing, and implementing new processes, and leading change management to drive adoption. Document processes, create workflow diagrams and clear visuals to support operational improvements and stakeholder understanding. Assist with building and scaling a system for managing legal requests across the company. Ensure intake, routing, prioritization, and tracking are seamless and visible. Work closely with other departments to ensure legal processes align with how the business operates.  Own and maintain legal knowledge spaces (e.g., on the company’s intranet) by keeping them organized, current, and easy to navigate.  Legal Billing & Budget Management Oversee the e-billing and matter management system, including onboarding vendors, fielding questions, and collecting accruals. Develop and maintain relationships with law firm billing departments, and review outside counsel invoices for compliance with billing guidelines. Assist with managing the department budget. Technology & Vendor Management Partner with our paralegal to own the legal tech stack – managing tools like Ironclad, DocuSign, etc.  Leverage AI to automate workflows and reduce manual work.  Research, evaluate, and recommend emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools, to improve efficiency.  Reporting & Analytics Assist Legal leaders in developing and implementing metrics and benchmarking to measure and report on team performance. Oversee the creation of regular, executive-level performance reports and presentations on legal department efficiencies, achievements, and value creation. General Responsibilities Operate with a strong bias for action, proactively identifying opportunities, driving initiatives forward independently, and exercising sound judgment on when to escalate things. Proactively engage with the legal operations community, industry forums, and vendor networks to identify emerging best practices and recommend improvements to our legal operations function. You may be asked to take on other tasks as assigned by Legal leadership.

job.title: Senior Coordinator, Media Operations
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is seeking a Sr. Coordinator, Media Operations to help deliver best-in-class media operations across the Federation’s 27 National Teams and major events, with a primary focus on the U.S. Men’s and Women’s National Teams.


Reporting to the Vice President, Communications, this role will be responsible for planning and executing media operations for National Team matches, camps, tournaments and other Federation events. The Sr. Coordinator will serve as a key operational contact for media and work closely with National Team press officers, Sporting, Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Commercial and venue partners to ensure media needs are thoughtfully planned and seamlessly executed.


The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented and comfortable working in fast-paced, high-profile environments. This individual should understand the needs of working media, anticipate operational challenges and be able to independently manage multiple priorities and stakeholders while delivering a consistent, professional media experience.


The Sr. Coordinator will work cross-functionally with Communications, Sporting, Event Operations, Media, Security, Ticketing and venue partners to ensure media requirements are integrated into event planning and that U.S. Soccer delivers a consistent, professional media experience across its National Teams and events.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate and execute media operations for U.S. Soccer National Team matches, camps, tournaments and Federation events, with primary focus on the Men’s and Women’s National Teams and support across all 27 National Teams as needed.
  • Manage media accreditation from application through event-day execution, including reviewing requests, assigning appropriate access, credential production and distribution, and troubleshooting accreditation issues.
  • Serve as a primary onsite point of contact for credentialed media, providing timely information, responding to questions and resolving operational issues.
  • Coordinate media facilities and operational requirements, including press boxes, media workrooms, press conference areas, mixed zones, photographer work areas and field-level positions, media entrances, connectivity, catering and other event-specific needs; manage photographer access and credential/bib distribution as required.
  • Manage media access and movement throughout venues, ensuring credentialed media are appropriately positioned, and event-specific access policies are followed.
  • Partner with venues and internal stakeholders in advance of matches and events to assess media infrastructure, determine operational needs and develop event-specific media operations plans; conduct pre-event walkthroughs and readiness checks to ensure media facilities, signage, technology and services meet established standards.
  • Partner closely with National and Youth Teams press officer to support player and coach media availability, live and virtual press conferences, training access and other team communications needs.
  • Develop and distribute media advisories and operational communications with accreditation details, schedules, access information, parking, media availability and other event logistics. Schedule virtual press conferences, provide links and meeting invites to all pertinent parties, and assist in execution.
  • Ensure U.S. Soccer Media Guidelines and event-specific access policies are consistently implemented, creating a professional working environment for journalists while protecting team needs and the rights of U.S. Soccer’s media partners.
  • Research local media markets and maintain accurate media lists and databases to support National Team and Federation communications efforts.
  • Build and maintain relationships with media operations contacts at venues, FIFA Member Associations, confederations and other soccer organizations.
  • Recruit, brief, train and manage event-day media volunteers, develop staffing plans and assignments, and establish clear roles, expectations and escalation procedures for each event.
  • Manage media operations equipment and inventory to ensure appropriate resources are available for National Team matches and events.
  • Manage media operations vendors, including sourcing services, negotiating agreements, tracking expenses and processing invoices within established budgets.
  • Collaborate with Event Operations, Broadcast, Security, Ticketing, Commercial and other internal teams to ensure media requirements are incorporated into overall event planning.
  • Help develop and implement consistent media operations standards, processes and best practices across U.S. Soccer’s National Teams.
  • Support media operations planning and execution for major international tournaments and other high-profile events hosted or supported by U.S. Soccer.
  • Anticipate operational challenges and independently troubleshoot issues in real time during matches and events.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
  • 3 to 5 years of relevant experience in media operations, communications, public relations, sports communications, event operations or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting media operations at major live sporting events; experience in professional or international soccer strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of media operations, accreditation and credentialing processes, venue access and the needs of working journalists, photographers and broadcasters.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage event logistics and multiple stakeholders in fast-paced, high-pressure environments.
  • Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, staffing plans, vendors and multiple concurrent workstreams.
  • Strong judgment and demonstrated ability to anticipate issues, solve problems and make decisions in live-event environments.
  • Strong service orientation and demonstrated ability to anticipate and respond to the needs of media and other event stakeholders.
  • Exceptional organizational and time-management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple events, deadlines and priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with media, athletes, coaches, executives, venue personnel and other high-profile stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office; experience with media accreditation, credentialing or event management platforms strongly preferred.
  • Spanish-language proficiency strongly preferred.
  • Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time and work nontraditional hours, including evenings, weekends and holidays, as needed.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. job.title: Pro License Educator
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


U.S. Soccer is looking for a Pro License Coach Educator to facilitate the U.S. Soccer Pro License and support the continued development of coaches working at the highest levels of the professional game. 


The ideal candidate combines significant experience in the professional game with expertise in player development and coach education. They understand the realities and demands of professional coaching and can create meaningful learning experiences that connect course learning with each student’s professional environment.


Working with the Pro License Technical Lead, this role will guide students through course learning, application in their club environments, feedback, reflection, and assessment. The Pro License Coach Educator will report to the Senior Director of Coaching Education and work closely with the Coach Education technical and operational staff, the Sporting Department, professional leagues and clubs, Coach Educators, mentors, and specialist contributors.


The role will also work closely with the Head of Continuous Professional Development to create and facilitate development opportunities that respond to the evolving needs of Pro-level coaches and the professional game


Primary Responsibilities

  

Pro License Course

  • Facilitate the Pro License curriculum across in-person and virtual learning experiences, mentoring, club visits, and application within students’ professional environments
  • Contribute to the continued improvement of the Pro License through insights from students, course delivery, research, and developments within the professional game

Student Learning & Development

  • Understand each student’s context, experience, strengths, and development needs
  • Build effective relationships and facilitate dialogue, reflection, and reality-based learning grounded in professional practices
  • Help students identify a development focus, apply learning in their club environment, gather evidence of their practice, and reflect on what they learn

Assessment & Mentoring

  • Observe professional practice, provide meaningful feedback, and support students and mentors
  • Document evidence of student learning and contribute to assessment and reassessment decisions in line with Pro License standards and processes
  • Contribute to consistency in assessment and Coach Educator practice across the Pro License

Player Development and the Professional Game

  • Bring current expertise in player development and the men’s and women’s professional game to connect individual and team development, game models, coaching processes, and performance demands
  • Adapt learning to the distinct player development, performance, and working environments across the men’s and women’s professional game
  • Ensure learning remains relevant to the evolving realities of professional soccer in the United States

Research, Innovation, and Continuous Professional Development

  • Stay current with research, innovation, emerging practice, and developments within the professional game
  • In collaboration with the Head of Continuous Professional Development, translate relevant research and emerging practice into meaningful development opportunities for Pro-level coaches   

Professional Partnerships

  • Build productive relationships across U.S. Soccer and with MLS, NWSL, USL, professional clubs, technical leaders, researchers, and specialists
  • Use these relationships to strengthen learning, connect education with the professional game, and provide students with access to relevant expertise and professional environments

Professional Standards

  • Model the professional standards expected of U.S. Soccer Coach Educators, including safeguarding, inclusion, confidentiality, professional integrity, and responsible handling of student and club information

Requirements


Qualifications

  • Coaching Certification: U.S. Soccer Pro License or other confederation Pro License required
  • Education:  Bachelor’s degree in Coaching, Coach Education, Sport Science, High-Performance Coaching, Education, Adult Learning, or a related field preferred
  • Experience: Significant experience in professional coaching, technical leadership, player development, coach education, or high-performance environments.
  • Travel: Ability to travel nationally, conduct club visits, and work evenings and weekends when required by course delivery and the professional-game calendar.
  • Language: English required; Spanish proficiency is a plus
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States


Candidate Profile

We are looking for an experienced professional who can operate credibly across professional soccer and coach education. The successful candidate will bring:

  • Significant experience within professional soccer and a strong understanding of the realities and demands facing coaches, players, staff, and clubs
  • Deep expertise in player development and the ability to connect individual player development with team development, the game model, training, competition, and the wider performance environment
  • Current understanding of the men’s and women’s professional game in the United States, including MLS, NWSL, USL, their clubs, player pathways, competitive environments, and evolving coaching demands
  • Strong understanding of the women’s professional game and considerations relevant to female player development
  • Experience as a Coach Educator, including facilitating adult learning, mentoring coaches, observing professional practice, providing feedback, and contributing to assessment
  • Sound judgment in evaluating professional practice against defined standards, using evidence to support fair and consistent assessment
  • Ability to build trust and engage experienced professional coaches in meaningful dialogue, reflection, and learning
  • Curiosity about the game and a commitment to research, innovation, and continuous learning
  • Ability to translate research, emerging practice, and developments in the professional game into relevant learning experiences for coaches
  • Strong relationship-building and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across U.S. Soccer and with professional leagues, clubs, technical leaders, researchers, and specialists


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Counsel, Technology & Privacy
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

The Senior Counsel, Technology & Privacy is a new role at U.S. Soccer and will be responsible for developing, supporting and advancing U.S. Soccer’s data governance program with a focus on privacy, data protection, and product counseling. Reporting to the Deputy General Counsel, Commercial & Business Affairs, you will provide practical, risk-based guidance, lead critical privacy and data initiatives, and build systems that enable U.S. Soccer to innovate responsibly while meeting evolving regulatory and ecosystem expectations. 


The ideal candidate brings deep privacy expertise, sound business judgment and experience operating with autonomy in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. The ideal candidate will also have experience counseling product, engineering and technical teams, translating complex privacy requirements into practical guidance, and supporting a fast-paced, technology-forward business. 


Primary Responsibilities


Privacy & Data Protection Counseling

  • Monitor and assess evolving privacy and data protection laws, regulatory guidance, and enforcement trends, and advise on impacts to the business
  • Assess U.S. Soccer’s compliance posture under applicable privacy and data protection laws and lead the development and maintenance of scalable governance processes, documentation standards, monitoring approaches, and reporting practices 
  • Provide practical, business-focused guidance on the collection, use, sharing, retention and protection of personal data and health data across U.S. Soccer’s products and operations
  • Respond to data sharing and ecosystem questions, including governance and contractual expectations
  • Support the company’s data governance uplift efforts, including roadmap development, milestone tracking, stakeholder alignment, and executive reporting
  • Working cross-functionally with the IT and Product teams, advise on, develop, and deliver privacy training and awareness; identify training needs, define content expectations and target audiences, create/update course materials

Product & Technology Counseling

  • Partner closely with the Product, IT, Sporting and Soccer Services teams to embed privacy considerations into the design, development, and deployment of products and platforms, with the goal of implementing practical, scalable controls across the product lifecycle
  • Review and advise on privacy implications of new products, features, technologies, and data uses, including conducting and supporting privacy impact and risk assessments
  • Counsel on data-driven initiatives, including analytics, marketing technologies, and emerging technologies such as AI, from a privacy and data governance perspective


Commercial & Vendor Support

  • Draft, review and negotiate a wide variety of technology and data-related agreements, including SaaS agreements, cloud services agreements, software development and licensing agreements, master services agreements, statements of work, and technology integration, data processing, and information security agreements. 
  • Review, draft and negotiate privacy and data protection provisions in commercial agreements, including data processing agreements and vendor contracts.


Regulatory & Risk Management

  • Own the cybersecurity and privacy legal strategy and operating model; establish standards, playbooks, escalation paths, and risk tolerances aligned to company goals
  • Advise on responses to data subject requests, regulatory inquiries, and privacy-related incidents 
  • Lead legal readiness for enterprise incident response (tabletops, playbooks, training) and advise on third-party breach response; serve as lead legal point of contact for significant cybersecurity incidents and privacy incidents
  • Lead regulatory readiness, audits, and internal assessments related to privacy and data security compliance


Other Transactional Support

  • As time permits, assist other transactional lawyers by drafting, reviewing and negotiating a variety of agreements in support of our business operations, including services agreements, event-related agreements, content acquisition agreements, licensing, and facility-related agreements
  • Assist other transactional lawyers in developing and maintaining contract templates and playbooks to streamline technology and other contract processes


Expectations of all members of our Legal & Corporate Affairs Department

  • Be a supportive mentor: share professional and industry knowledge generously, provide active guidance on professional development to staff that is more junior to you, and contribute to a culture of intellectual curiosity and high standards
  • Provide thought leadership with respect to legal operations, including how to create efficiencies, use technology, serve our internal clients better, and control costs 
  • Contribute to the creation and maintenance of our standard forms library 
  • Treat others with respect, kindness, patience and empathy 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  •  J.D. from an accredited law school and an active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, in good standing
  • Minimum 8-10 years of legal experience, with a significant focus on privacy, data protection, and technology-related matters
  • Demonstrated experience providing product counseling and advising engineering, product and technical teams
  • Solid understanding of data protection, cybersecurity and information security principles
  • Minimum 5 years in-house experience 
  • Sports industry experience preferred, but not required
  • Experience in an engineering or technical project management role preferred, but not required 
  • Strong ability to translate complex legal and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance for technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Knowledge of HIPAA and other healthcare privacy requirements preferred
  • Familiarity with security frameworks and control environments (NIST, ISO 27001) 
  • Experience designing and implementing policies, standards, controls, and metrics in a complex organization 
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Exceptional drafting, negotiation, analytical and communication skills
  • High level of commitment to quality work product and organizational ethics, integrity and compliance
  • General knowledge of soccer
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)



U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

- As time permits, assist other transactional lawyers by drafting, reviewing and negotiating a variety of agreements in support of our business operations, including services agreements, event-related agreements, content acquisition agreements, licensing, and facility-related agreements - Assist other transactional lawyers in developing and maintaining contract templates and playbooks to streamline technology and other contract processes
Expectations ofallmembers of our Legal & Corporate Affairs Department
- Be a supportive mentor: share professional and industry knowledge generously, provide active guidance on professional development to staff that is more junior to you, and contribute to a culture of intellectual curiosity and high standards - Provide thought leadership with respect to legal operations, including how to create efficiencies, use technology, serve our internal clients better, and control costs - Contribute to the creation and maintenance of our standard forms library - Treat others with respect, kindness, patience and empathy
Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
- J.D. from an accredited law school and an active license to practice law in at least one U.S. jurisdiction, in good standing - Minimum 8-10 years of legal experience, with a significant focus on privacy, data protection, and technology-related matters - Demonstrated experience providing product counseling and advising engineering, product and technical teams - Solid understanding of data protection, cybersecurity and information security principles - Minimum 5 years in-house experience - Sports industry experience preferred, but not required - Experience in an engineering or technical project management role preferred, but not required - Strong ability to translate complex legal and regulatory requirements into clear, actionable guidance for technical and non-technical stakeholders - Knowledge of HIPAA and other healthcare privacy requirements preferred - Familiarity with security frameworks and control environments (NIST, ISO 27001) - Experience designing and implementing policies, standards, controls, and metrics in a complex organization - Excellent communication, collaboration, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment - Exceptional drafting, negotiation, analytical and communication skills - High level of commitment to quality work product and organizational ethics, integrity and compliance - General knowledge of soccer - Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments - Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission - Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)
U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.

job.title: Coordinator, Talent Identification Operations
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Coordinator, Talent Identification Operations is responsible for providing administrative support to the Talent ID Leadership, Remote Talent ID Managers, YNT Talent Scouts, and Talent Reporters to?efficiently organize and execute all processes and special projects.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Commits to the mission, objectives, and policies of U.S. Soccer 
  • Applies U.S. Soccer Talent Identification Philosophy, Framework, Processes and Structures 
  • Communicates effectively with all stakeholders (staff, scouts, coaches, members, clubs, parents, etc.) involved in talent identification 
  • Coordinates all Talent ID procedures to support YNT Scouting and all other strategic components 
  • Initiate, research, analyze, and interpret various data sets to provide Talent ID insights
  • Help Regional Talent ID Managers plan and execute Talent ID Centers (Invites, RSVPS, Facility Comms, Referees, ATC, video, etc.)
  • Provide support to YNT Talent Scouts (onboarding, travel, reimbursements, equipment, resources, payroll, compliance, etc.)
  • Update digital platforms and Player Monitoring System (P3) (player adds, club recommendations, player transfers, club/player contact info, dual/multiple nationalities, etc.)
  • Fielding all external scouting inquiries (scouting@ussoccer.org, talentreporters@ussoccer.org) and responding/filtering appropriately? 
  • Compile, create, and distribute scouting, YNT, and market analysis data to internal/external stakeholders 
  • Help managers plan and execute U14 Regional and National TID Camps (Hotels, Invites, RSVPS, Staff, Facility Comms, Refs, etc.
  • Plan and execute Talent ID’s attendance at specified league events (hotels, travel, league communication, player review meetings, etc.)
  • Provide Extended National Teams Talent ID Manager with operational support
  • Provide operational support to Talent ID Education and Talent Reporters Program which could include report analysis, compliance, webinar support, special projects, etc. 
  • Support Talent ID initiatives and specialized projects 
  • Invest in U.S. Soccer’s goal setting process by taking ownership of and routinely assessing ongoing personal development plan, including creation of annual individual goals.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher
  • Strong knowledge of soccer landscape in the U.S. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication combined with a professional demeanor 
  • Customer service focus to solve complex and urgent situations 
  • Exceptional attention to detail 
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments
  • Ability to deliver high-quality work and execute under pressure and deadlines 
  • Exceptional time management skills and ability to prioritize workflow  
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills
  • Proficient experience with other Microsoft Suite products (Word, PowerPoint, Sharepoint, and Outlook)
  • Able and willing to travel up to 15% of the year 
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours including evenings and weekends as needed


Desired Qualifications

  • Passion for soccer
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish)
  • Experience in developing/supporting technology platforms or database management 
  • Knowledge with soccer scouting and data platforms (Wyscout, Opta, Hudl, Sportscode, etc.)  
  • Proficiency with numerical analysis and/or data visualization platform (R, Tableau, SQL, etc.)    
  • Previous scouting operations experience with a club or national team



U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Head of Recruitment
job.html_description:
Head of Recruitment

A great opportunity has arisen to work here at Wolverhampton Wanderers as Head of Recruitment.

The Head of Recruitment is responsible for leading the club's player identification & recruitment strategy across first team, academy & emerging talent pathways working in conjunction with the Head of Academy Recruitment. The role ensures the club identifies, evaluates & acquires players who align with the club's performance objectives, financial parameters, and long-term succession planning.

Working closely with the Technical Director, Head Coach, Performance Analysis department, Loans Department and his/her Recruitment Team, the Head of Recruitment will oversee domestic and international scouting operations, player identification processes and data-driven recruitment methodologies.

For more details on the role and it's requirements, please see the below job description.

Ref: MJ-00-29092026

Closing date: 5th November 2026
